[1] Гуль (Ghoul) L21 [Мифологическое описание]
Its exact appearance is not known, because later, "Khephren the Great, who raised the Second Pyramid, carved over the Sphinx’s face in the likeness of his own." In 1910, the magician Harry Houdini glimpsed the Unknown God of the Dead after being imprisoned in an unknown temple hundreds of feet below the Gizeh plateau, and perhaps constituting an undiscovered lower level of the Temple of the Sphinx near the Second Pyramind. The thing was being worshipped by hybrid men with the heads of hippos or crocodiles, along with King Khephren (aka the guide Abdul Reis el Drogman) and the ghoul-queen Nitokris. As it emerged from a huge dark doorway, the Unknown One appeared at first to be something yellowish and hairy, about the size of a hippopotamus, with five heads from which curious rigid tentacles extended to seize large offerings of carrion. Soon after, Houdini realized that this creature was the merest forepaw of a much larger being, presumably with an overall form resembling the Sphinx. Ever since the first hint of dawn, he had lain there, watching the cabin. A heavy rifle lay beneath his arm.

FILE: 'Twas the Night Before Madness.txt
Mentions: 1/1 | d:10.3/10k

[1] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L53 [Ритуал и призывание]
Alessandro Martinez. It was published in the Jesse Dedman William C. Marchese -edited anthology Cthulhu Christmas Special and Other Lovecraftian Yuletide Tales in November 2017. Synopsis The twelve four-line verses describe how, at Christmas time, a cultist conducts a murderous ritual to summon the Old Ones to our plane of existence. As they return to the material realm, they grant him incredible knowledge, but shatter his sanity in the process. Trivia The entities summoned by the cultist include Yog-Sothoth Dagon Hastur Yig Gla'aki Cthulhu Ithaqua Nyarlathotep , and Cthylla

[1] Йог-Сотот ('Umr at-Tawil) L1 [Энциклопедическая статья]
НАЗВАНИЕ: 'Umr at-Tawil (Cthulhu Universalis) ИСТОЧНИК: 'Umr at-Tawil A being who lives in the First Gateway , at the transdimensional extension of earth which is outside time, and serves as a Guide to the next, or Ultimate Gate . 'Umr at-Tawil is the leader of the Ancient Ones (1) , who are manifestations of Yog-Sothoth . 'Umr at-Tawil had been an entity of earth millions of years ago, long before humanity, at the time of the earliest mammals.

[2] Йог-Сотот ('Umr at-Tawil) L23

'Umr at-Tawil is heavily cloaked, apparently shaped something like a man, but changeable in shape and half again as large; it moves by gliding or floating.

Lovecraft and E. Hoffmann Price in their short story " Through the Gates of the Silver Key Background 'Umr at-Tawil is an entity who stands beside the Ultimate Gate , meeting any who traverse the first Gate via the Silver Key . He appears as a heavily cloaked figure with no organs or features discernible beneath his garb. It is somewhat humanoid in shape, but "half as large again as an ordinary man", and moves about by gliding or floating over the ground.

[3] Йог-Сотот ('Umr at-Tawil) L135 [Гримуар]
Abdul Alhazred , in the Necronomicon , identifies this entity as "the Most Ancient One" and "the Prolonged of Life", and cites the Book of Thoth 's claim about a "terrific" price to be paid by those who glimpse at it. Believed to have originated as a prehistoric Earth creature that inhabited the planet long before the dawn of humanity , 'Umr at-Tawil is the leader of the Ancient Ones , which are manifestations of the All-in-One and One-in-All, speculated to be Yog-Sothoth by Randolph Carter HPL Through the Gates of the Silver Key At least one ancient book claimed that 'Umr at-Tawil and the Ancient Ones were agents of Yog-Sothoth, identified as the All-in-One and One-in-All, and that they "dream forever of that time when once again they shall rule to whom rightfully belong Earth and the entire universe of which it is a part".

[4] Йог-Сотот ('Umr at-Tawil) L159 [Мифологическое описание]
( AWD The House on Curwen Street Pathfinder 'Umr at-Tawil appears as a Great Old One in the role-playing game Pathfinder , under the name Tawil at'Umr In the Pathfinder multiverse, Tawil at'Umr is a servant of Yog-Sothoth, operating as the physical projection of its will and working towards its agenda across the dimensions. Tawil at'Umr is theorized on Golarion to being the side of effect of Yog-Sothoth's contact with the material plane. Its knowledge about reality is vast, including how one may access the Dimension of Time, but one acquires such knowledge at a terrible cost.

[1] Тьма (Darkness) L171 [Художественный сюжет]
His Mystic Analectica is a voluminous compendium of sage epistles, Containing an entire section on -- The Black Stone of the Thistles. Black Stone of Thistles I shudder to tell, Devil stone of troubles by power of hell. Dug from the ground in the farmer's field, After countless long ages again reveal'd. Polish'd black surface cover'd with runes, It's secret is known to him that communes With the hidden ONE of the unknown; He shall learn the secrets of the stone -- Then cometh the revelation of darkness, Yea, the desolation of boundless darkness. Thus begins Carlo Dombretì's esoteric section on the Black Stone, Indeed, understood by very few and by most completely unknown; The Analectica reveals that the stone was rediscovered on a fief, When, while tilling, an unlearned peasant (who was devout in belief) Uncover'd the stone that was an evil omen of cataclysmic events. Dombretì says 'its arcane cryptographic markings defied all sense', Until Robert Griffen, 'bout whom many strange things are said, Studied the weird runes but wisely left what he learned unsaid.

НАЗВАНИЕ: A Handful of Dust ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:11:16 СИМВОЛОВ: 1419 A Handful of Dust Author David Conyers Language English Series Call of Cthulhu Genre(s) Roleplaying game Publisher Yog-Sothoth. com Release Date Preceded by Devil's Children A Handful of Dust: The Witch Cycle Part 2 is a scenario supplement for the Delta Green setting of Chaosium Call of Cthulhu roleplaying game. FILE: A Note on the Cthulhu Mythos.txt
Mentions: 1/1 | d:4.46/10k

[1] Тьма (Darkness) L69 [Мифологическое описание]
P. Lovecraft , its basic themes and most important deities, and how the system has been developed gradually. Although he cautions that there is "no hard and fast line separating Lovecraft's Dunsanian tales from the stories which are definitely part of the Mythos ", Derlerth defines the latter as consisting primarily of 13 Lovecraft stories: " The Nameless City The Festival The Call of Cthulhu " (in which he claims the Mythos gained "its first indication of shape"), " The Colour Out of Space The Dunwich Horror The Whisperer in Darkness The Dreams in the Witch-House The Haunter of the Dark The Shadow Over Innsmouth The Shadow Out of Time At the Mountains of Madness The Case of Charles Dexter Ward , and " The Thing on the Doorstep Controversially, Derleth ascribes to Lovecraft the idea that the Mythos revolves around an age-old conflict between the Elder Gods , which represent order, and the Great Old Ones , their enemies, which represent "the forces of evil". In truth, this concept is not explicitly present anywhere in Lovecraft's works, although it is present in Derleth's own Mythos stories, some of which were published while Lovecraft was still alive and the two authors corresponded frequently. On a less controversial note, Derleth also defends Lovecraft from the attacks of Colin Wilson and other critics, and ensures that the author saw his work for what it was: fiction, intended "for his own entertainment" as well as his readers'.

Price . It was published in the Matthew Carpenter -edited thematic anthology Pickman's Gallery by Ulthar Press in 2018. Synopsis Detective Thomas Malone is assigned to investigate the disappearance of the eccentric Bostonian artist Richard Upton Pickman . After interviewing his associate Thurber (whose first name Price gives as Ethan) the two take a trip to Pickman's studio, and the two investigate a suspicious well in the basement. Traversing the seemingly-endless stairs contained within, they find themselves in the Dreamlands , and quickly happen upon Pickman himself. For an unexplained reason, Pickman transforms himself into a ghoul and kills Thurber, though Malone manages to escape and presumably make his way back to the waking world. Behind the Mythos Thomas Malone is possibly the character created by H. P. Lovecraft for his 1927 short story " The Horror at Red Hook ", although this is never confirmed. If this is the case, whether the story takes place before or after the events described in "The Horror at Red Hook" is uncertain, although it seems likely to be the latter.

It was published in the Matthew Carpenter -edited anthology Pickman's Gallery by Ulthar Press in 2018. Synopsis Wealthy art lover Walter, a man with an obsessional interest in the vanished artist Richard Upton Pickman , learns that a previously-unseen collection of Pickman's works has come up for sale. He quickly contacts the seller and buys the works, one of which is wrapped in protective paper and accompanied by a note warning of dire consequences should anyone look upon it. When Walter gets the piece home, he peels off the covering and admires at the work, titled The Witch of Copp's Hill , which shows a picture of a pack of ghouls cavorting in a cemetery no more than a mile from Walter's home. As he looks on, the picture begins to change, with the ghouls tearing a victim to pieces and prostrating themselves in front of a mysterious woman, before turning to stare directly at him. Determined to prove to himself that what he had just witnessed was a hallucination, Walter makes his way to the cemetery. However, upon his arrival he discovers to his horror that what he witnessed was no mere hallucination, but a vision of his fate.

P. Lovecraft Abbith , a. k. a. the World of Seven Suns , is a fictional planet that revolves around seven stars beyond Xoth . It is inhabited by Metallic Brains , wise with the ultimate secrets of the universe. Nyarlathotep dwells or is imprisoned on this planet. Behind the Mythos While the "world of Seven Suns" was referenced as the abode of Nyarlathotep by H. P. Lovecraft HPL The Whisperer in Darkness ) and August Derleth AWD The Dweller in Darkness "), the name Abbith was created by Lin Carter A place called Cytharion of the Seven Suns is mentioned by Lovecraft in " The Crawling Chaos ". However, in spite of its title, that story doesn't feature Nyarlathotep. In Carter's works, Abbith is also identified as a world revolving around Algol , which is the abode of Zvilpogghua in " The Feaster from the Stars ". However, this identification only occurs in the revised version of the story, as published in The Book of Eibon . In the version published in the Crypt of Cthulhu magazine, the Algolian world inhabited by Zvilpogghua is instead identified as Ymar, whereas another story identifies it as Yrautrom.

НАЗВАНИЕ: Aletheia ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:11:39 СИМВОЛОВ: 6267 Aletheia Origin Z'lyeh First appearance EXP Dylan Dog 374 "La Fine dell'Oscurità" Created by Tiziano Sclavi Aletheia is a fictional deity created by comic book author Tiziano Sclavi for Dylan Dog issue #374 "La Fine dell'Oscuritó" (Sergio Bonelli Editore, November 2017). Description Aletheia appears as a large loosely interconnected grouping of enormous hands in the sky, jutting out of clouds and darkness, with each hand having a large eye in the center of its palm. Untold amounts of much smaller but thick cords or threads of metallic flesh extend from the surface of its hands and fingers - the threads of Aletheia. A thread of Aletheia will interconnect with a human victim at the base of their spine. Attempting to remove the thread - which is about as thick as the spine it attached itself to - with sufficient force will cause the entire spine of the victim to be violently pulled out, leading to an explosively gory demise.

[2] Тьма (Darkness) L87 [Ритуал и призывание]
The only account of these events are Dylan Dog's writings themselves, as others have begun to forget the events entirely and the summoner's fate is unknown. Since Dylan Dog was himself affected by Aletheia, it is unclear what the actual or current status, if any, of the deity is, given its paradoxical vision of reality which Dylan Dog (and maybe only himself) believes to be the truth. Behind the Mythos Aletheia is the greek word for "truth"; etymologically it transliterates as "uncovered" or "unforgotten". The title of the story, La Fine dell'Oscuritó (The End of Darkness) furthermore plays on the useage of light in portrayals of truth in both the story and our world. Despite being summoned using the R'lyehian invocation " Ph'nglui mglw'nafh Aletheia Z'lyeh wgah'nagl fhtagn! ", Aletheia's connection to the Cthulhu Mythos is not entirely clear.

In " The Feaster from the Stars ", Carter identifies it as either Ymar (in the Crypt of Cthulhu version) or Abbith (in the Book of Eibon version), the latter being Carter's name for the World of Seven Suns from which Nyarlathotep can be summoned (as mentioned in Lovecraft's The Whisperer in Darkness and August Derleth 's " The Dweller in Darkness "). FILE: Alien (franchise).txt
Mentions: 1/1 | d:1.59/10k

[1] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L89 [Мифологическое описание]
The series has also crossed over with other popular properties, including The Terminator Marvel Comics The Avengers Vampirella Judge Dredd , D. C. Comics' Batman and Superman Buffy the Vampire Slayer , and Predator . The latter, launched in 1990 by Dark Horse Comics in Dark Horse Presents and supported by an Easter egg in the film Predator 2 the same year, has established itself as a long-term interaction between the two properties. Although featuring little in the way of specific references to either the works of H. P. Lovecraft or the Cthulhu Mythos in general, the Alien franchise was intended to have a more direct connection from its inception, with writer Dan O'Bannon's early screenplay showing the titular aliens as having a connection to the Outer God Yog-Sothoth Despite this having been written out in the final draft, the finished film has been cited as a prime example of cosmic horror in cinema, Elements and Themes Central to the franchise's stories are the titular aliens, most commonly referred to as Xenomorphs since the release of the first sequel film, Aliens , in 1986. These creatures are multi-stage, insect-like parasitic lifeforms which require a living host in which to gestate; birth invariably results in the death of the host. The Xenomorphs are highly-aggressive, lethal predators who will do anything to protect their hive colonies, and possess a defence mechanism in the form of acid blood, meaning that even in death, a Xenomorph has the potential to eliminate its opponent.

P. Lovecraft Dreamlands . The story was first published in 1995 in the magazine Crypt of Cthulhu , and is also included in Cannon's 2011 collection Forever Azathoth: Parodies and Pastiches Synopsis James Herriot is a veterinary surgeon working in the Dreamlands who has treated all sorts of species, from Ghouls to Wamps . One day, King Kuranes calls him to look at his beloved Moon-beast , Matilda, a strong and healthy racer, now suddenly looking ill, with her pink tentacles turned to a sickly shade of green. Herriot prescribes an ointment, but with little success: a few days later, a distressed Kuranes appears in the clinic with Matilda looking worse than before. Herriot and fellow doctor Siegfried Farnon try to get the Moon-beast to consume the prescribed medicine by offering it inside the body of a tasty Zoog .

[2] Йог-Сотот ('Umr at-Tawil) L101 [Мифологическое описание]
In the final version, their physical appearance is concealed by the hooded cloaks they wear. The Ancient Ones dwell in an "extension" of planet Earth , in a realm where time has no meaning. Randolph Carter met these beings when he used the Silver Key to cross through the First Gate . At first, Carter perceived them as "cloaked, ill-defined Shapes" standing on hieroglyphed quasi-hexagonal giant pedestals. They are led by 'Umr at-Tawil , who is known as the Most Ancient One, a vaguely humanoid being believed to have once been a creature that inhabited the Earth long before the rise of humankind . As Carter soon learns, the Ancient Ones are, in fact, manifestations of the All-in-One and One-in-All, the Supreme Archetype, which he believes to be Yog-Sothoth When Carter approached the Ultimate Gate , the forms of the Ancient Ones became clearer and more human-like to him, even though Carter was aware that they were not human.

НАЗВАНИЕ: Animus ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:11:50 СИМВОЛОВ: 1905 Animus Also known as Pwodarauk Lloigor Affiliations Great Old Ones First appearance ADJ : "The Web Planet" Created by Bill Strutton The Animus is an extraterrestrial life form created by the BBC for Doctor Who in 1965. It was the only one of its race to cross into the physical universe, establishing itself at Vortis and turning the formerly lush planet into an acidic wasteland. It manifested itself within the Carsenome, an organic self-healing palace. The Animus is capable of taking over anything living which came into contact with gold. It resembled a hybrid created by crossing a spider or plant with an octopus. It could generate a fungus-like sustenance which grew into Carsenome, its fortress.

Горта, шатаясь, спустился по ступеням и завопил в бесконечность замерзшей пустоты, простершейся перед ним, что он найдет путь домой. Но вместо того, чтобы перед ним возник образ Винтербурга или даже Муркара, тьма оставалась неизменной. Вместо этого он почувствовал, как в стенах покинутого города поднимается присутствие страшного зла. Горта воззвал к темным теням, умоляя оставить его в покое. Он упал на колени и пополз прочь по глубокому снегу. Он не имел ни малейшего понятия, куда направляется и что надеется там найти. Когда он обернулся и взглянул на путь, который проложил сквозь снег, то не увидел никаких следов, лишь идеальную гладь нетронутой белизны.

Он опустился на троне и снова почувствовал, как его поглощает тьма. ГОРТА ПРОСНУЛСЯ и обнаружил, что лежит на спине на теплом, мягком ковре. Он перевернулся. Из-под двери валил дым. Дверная коробка только начинала заниматься, когда языки пламени лизнули ее основание. Он поднялся на ноги и рванул дверь на себя. Его королева не могла понять, почему температура его тела падала до опасно низкого уровня или почему, когда сильнейшие кошмары терзали его, он бредил на чуждом языке, который лингвисты Муркара были не в силах распознать.

An Egyptian cult of priest-sorcerers viewed their gods, including Anubis, as the representatives of actual Hidden Beings—monstrous beast-men who shambled on Earth in primal days [ RB Fane ]. Anubis is the Opener of the Way, jackal-headed god who guards cryptic Karneter, and holds the keys to Life and Death. He is not a friend of those who rule. He stands in shadows, for he is the Keeper of Mysteries. It is written that an evil priest called the Master carved the first statue of the true form of Anubis; and that the statue now guards the Master's tomb. Archeologists Ronald Barton and Peter Barton discovered the tomb and found two images of Anubis. The first was a silver symbol on a door, with the heads of seven principal Egyptian gods: Osiris Isis Ra Bast Thoth Set , and Anubis.

FILE: Archetypes (Cthulhu Universalis).txt
Mentions: 4/4 | d:12.85/10k

[1] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L7 [Энциклопедическая статья]
НАЗВАНИЕ: Archetypes (Cthulhu Universalis) ИСТОЧНИК: Archetypes Archetypes (1, of Yog-Sothoth) HPL Gates online text )]: People of the ultimate abyss, with an infinite number of dimensions, or perhaps existing outside all dimensions. They are "prodigious forms whose multiple extensions transcended any conception of being, size, and boundaries." They exist outside of time with no past, present, or future. Individuals in our world are each three-dimensional cross sections of one or another of the archetypes. Cross sections of the same archetype at different angles correspond to different individuals. Examples are Randolph Carter and the wizard Zkauba , who dwell in different solar systems, but who are both slices of the Yog-Sothoth archetype.

[2] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L27 [Энциклопедическая статья]
НАЗВАНИЕ: Archetypes (Cthulhu Universalis) ИСТОЧНИК: Archetypes Archetypes (1, of Yog-Sothoth) HPL Gates online text )]: People of the ultimate abyss, with an infinite number of dimensions, or perhaps existing outside all dimensions. They are "prodigious forms whose multiple extensions transcended any conception of being, size, and boundaries." They exist outside of time with no past, present, or future. Individuals in our world are each three-dimensional cross sections of one or another of the archetypes. Cross sections of the same archetype at different angles correspond to different individuals. Examples are Randolph Carter and the wizard Zkauba , who dwell in different solar systems, but who are both slices of the Yog-Sothoth archetype. Slight changes of the angle of a slice can also correspond to different stages in the life of a single individual, such as Randolph Carter. Of all the archetypes, Yog-Sothoth is supreme, and is the source of "all great wizards, all great thinkers, all great artists" on every world. Lovecraft and his coauthor, E. Hoffman Price, do not provide any information about the other archetypes. Since Yog-Sothoth is an archetype, it is conceivable that some of Lovecraft's other major beings are also archetypes.

[3] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L29 [Мифологическое описание]
They exist outside of time with no past, present, or future. Individuals in our world are each three-dimensional cross sections of one or another of the archetypes. Cross sections of the same archetype at different angles correspond to different individuals. Examples are Randolph Carter and the wizard Zkauba , who dwell in different solar systems, but who are both slices of the Yog-Sothoth archetype. Slight changes of the angle of a slice can also correspond to different stages in the life of a single individual, such as Randolph Carter. Of all the archetypes, Yog-Sothoth is supreme, and is the source of "all great wizards, all great thinkers, all great artists" on every world. Lovecraft and his coauthor, E. Hoffman Price, do not provide any information about the other archetypes. Since Yog-Sothoth is an archetype, it is conceivable that some of Lovecraft's other major beings are also archetypes. For example, Azathoth could be an archetype of dreamers or creators, Nyarlathotep could be the archetypal messenger, and Shub-Niggurath could be an archetype of fertility. The Other Gods could all be archetypes, or they could all be cross-sections of Azathoth. Cthulhu could be the archetype of priests.

[4] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L31 [Мифологическое описание]
Examples are Randolph Carter and the wizard Zkauba , who dwell in different solar systems, but who are both slices of the Yog-Sothoth archetype. Hoffman Price, do not provide any information about the other archetypes. Since Yog-Sothoth is an archetype, it is conceivable that some of Lovecraft's other major beings are also archetypes. The Other Gods could all be archetypes, or they could all be cross-sections of Azathoth. Cthulhu could be the archetype of priests. It is a disturbing cosmology, since it implies that we are each derived from one of these unspeakably alien beings, or at least that we have a common source with them. No information is presented about the appearance of these archetypes.

FILE: Arkham Gazette.txt
Mentions: 1/1 | d:5.96/10k

[1] Тьма (Darkness) L79 [Мифологическое описание]
P. Lovecraft The Arkham Gazette is a fictional newspaper created by H. P. Lovecraft for his Cthulhu Mythos stories. Overview The newspaper was created to service the fictional town of Arkham Massachusetts . Although Lovecraft created the Arkham Gazette , it plays no appreciable part in his stories. Later authors have included it in their works, however. The Gazette has been in circulation since at least the 1880s. In Lovecraft's works, it is only mentioned in " The Colour Out of Space ", which is set in 1883. In stories set in the early 20th century, such as " The Dunwich Horror The Whisperer in Darkness , and At the Mountains of Madness , the Arkham Advertiser is mentioned instead. In the works of August Derleth , it is confirmed that the Gazette still exists in the 1930s, as Andrew Phelan, while seeking information about his employer Prof. Shrewsbury , "sought the newspaper files of both the Arkham papers, the Gazette and the Advertiser AWD The House on Curwen Street Employees Willard Peck, editor ( EXP Bones of the Yopasi Tisha Hewitt EXP Beneath Cayuga's Churning Waves Trivia Named for the newspaper, The Arkham Gazette is a sporadically-released real-world zine created to supplement Chaosium Call of Cthulhu horror roleplaying game.

Overview The Second Edition Core Set had been quite drastically overhauled from the First Edition, with many major changes such as the removal of randomised movement rates and the addition of Ancient Ones to serve as final "bosses" for the Investigators. Bioshock Infinite : first-person roleplaying game whose main character, Booker Dewitt, is stated to come from Arkham. Call of Cthulhu: Dark Corners of the Earth : roleplaying game in which the main character, private detective Jack Walters, is admitted to the Arkham Mental Institution after seeing Yithians and going insane during a raid on a Boston home. Lovecraft himself appears as a professor at the university, conjuring demons for the heroes to fight at their request. Sherlock Holmes: The Awakened : a mystery game that combines the Cthulhu Mythos with Sherlock Holmes . The main villain mentions Arkham in the final confrontation. Splatterhouse : 2010 video game which takes place in the setting of Arkham, Massachusetts.

P. Lovecraft Arkham is a fictional town set in the US state of Massachusetts , invented by H. P. Lovecraft . It frequently appears in his horror fiction and in the work of other writers in the Cthulhu Mythos , particularly as the home of Miskatonic University , making it a key location in the Lovecraft Country setting. Arkham is the namesake of Arkham House , the publishing house that promoted Lovecraft's work after his death.

НАЗВАНИЕ: Arkham: Reanimated ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:11:57 СИМВОЛОВ: 6166 Arkham: Reanimated Author Brandon Berntson Country United States Language English Series The Lovecraft Mysteries Release Date February 2020 Pages Preceded by The Night of Dagon Followed by The Lurker at the Threshold Arkham: Reanimated is a Cthulhu Mythos novel by American author Brandon Berntson , the second in his Lovecraft Mysteries series. Running to a total of 168 pages, it was independently published in February 2020; both paperback and digital editions were released. Synopsis Millie Von Clydesburgh and Devlin Macky decide to take a day trip to the countryside, but become stranded in the near-derelict tumbledown that is Arkham . There, they encounter hostile locals, reanimated corpses , abominable experiments, and even an Outer God in their efforts to find out what secrets haunt the mysterious town.

Clarke . A parody of H. P. Lovecraft At the Mountains of Madness , it was first published in the March 1940 edition of fanzine The Satellite Synopsis The sole remaining survivor of an expedition to the Antarctic tells of how his group stumbled across the ancient civilisation of the Elder Ones, existing quietly for millennia beneath Mount Morgue. Although at first believing their hosts to be cultured and genial, the party soon come to the realisation that the Elder Ones wish to destroy the human race. Making a bid for freedom, they are pursued by the unspeakable creatures which serve the Elder Ones, but manage to effect their escape with the aid of a shoddily-repaired main gateway which buys them time to flee. Behind the Mythos "At the Mountains of Murkiness" contains many elements from Lovecraft's works, all of them altered or exaggerated for comedic effect. These include a creature which fits the description of a Shoggoth , ancient bas-reliefs which are hard for the human mind to look at, an ill-fated Antarctic expedition , and the Elder Ones themselves- who are mentioned to own a half interest in pulp magazine Weird Tales .

FILE: August Derleth_ posthumous collaboration controversy.txt
Mentions: 2/2 | d:4.46/10k

[1] Йог-Сотот (The Lurker at the Threshold) L55 [Гримуар]
P. Lovecraft and August Derleth," were in fact written almost entirely by Derleth. In most cases, the stories were based on one or more ideas noted in Lovecraft’s Commonplace Book ; for example, "The Fisherman of Falcon Point" was based on this entry: "Fisherman casts his net into the sea by moonlight—what he finds." Plotting, description, dialogue, characterization, and other elements were entirely by Derleth. As such they cannot be classified as works by Lovecraft. In some instances Derleth incorporated actual prose passages by Lovecraft into his stories. The Lurker at the Threshold (a 50,000-word novel) contains about 1,200 words by Lovecraft, most of it taken from a fragment entitled "Of Evill Sorceries Done in New England" (see B-i-42), the balance from a fragment now titled "The Rose Window" (see B-ii-322). "The Survivor" was based on a comparatively lengthy plot sketch plus random notes for the story jotted down by Lovecraft in 1934. A descriptive passage of "The Lamp of Alhazred" was based on a portion of a letter by Lovecraft to Derleth, 18 November 1936. These extracts or paraphrases, however, have not been deemed significant enough to merit inclusion in this bibliography. The 16 Stories The 16 stories that S. T.

[2] Йог-Сотот (The Lurker at the Threshold) L63 [Мифологическое описание]
"The Survivor" was based on a comparatively lengthy plot sketch plus random notes for the story jotted down by Lovecraft in 1934. A descriptive passage of "The Lamp of Alhazred" was based on a portion of a letter by Lovecraft to Derleth, 18 November 1936. These extracts or paraphrases, however, have not been deemed significant enough to merit inclusion in this bibliography. The 16 Stories The 16 stories that S. T. Joshi has separated apart, which have been in the past uncritically attributed to both Lovecraft and Derleth as co-authors, or even to Lovecraft alone, are: The Lurker at the Threshold (1945) The Survivor " (1954) The Ancestor " (1957) The Gable Window " (1957) The Lamp of Alhazred " (1957) The Peabody Heritage " (1957) The Shadow Out of Space " (1957) Wentworth's Day " (1957) The Fisherman of Falcon Point " (1959) The Shuttered Room " (1959) Witches' Hollow " (1962) The Shadow in the Attic " (1964) The Dark Brotherhood " (1966) The Horror from the Middle Span " (1974) Innsmouth Clay " (1974) The Watchers Out of Time " (1974, unfinished before Derleth's death in 1971) S. T. Joshi's scholarship confirmed what was known privately for many years, that none of the above works are by H. P. Lovecraft. All of them are properly to be considered entirely the works of August Derleth. This has no relevancy to any praise or criticism of these stories based on their merits; this is a matter completely related to authorship alone. Posthumous Collaboration: A Mythos Tradition?

FILE: Averoigne.txt
Mentions: 1/2 | d:2.5/10k

[1] Йог-Сотот (Iog-Sotôt) L75 [Мифологическое описание]
The fictional land appears to based on the historical province of Auvergne. The frequent references to Lovecraftian deities, often in transparently altered terms (Sodaqui for Tsathoggua , Iog-Sotôt for Yog-Sothoth , the Ram With a Thousand Ewes for Shub-Niggurath ), establish Averoigne as a part of the Cthulhu Mythos In addition to Mythos entities and their worshippers, Smith populates Averoigne with malign and dangerous creatures like vampires Rendezvous in Averoigne lamias The End of the Story ", possibly " The Enchantress of Sylaire "), and satyrs The Satyr Stories Smith used Averoigne as the setting for the following stories: The End of the Story Weird Tales , May 1930) A Rendezvous in Averoigne Weird Tales , April/May 1931) The Satyr La Paree Stories , July 1931) The Maker of Gargoyles Weird Tales , August 1932) The Mandrakes Weird Tales , February 1933) The Beast of Averoigne Weird Tales , May 1933) The Holiness of Azédarac Weird Tales , November 1933) The Colossus of Ylourgne Weird Tales , June 1934) The Disinterment of Venus Weird Tales , July 1934) Mother of Toads Weird Tales , July 1938) The Enchantress of Sylaire Weird Tales , July 1941) Averoigne " (poetry) ( Challenge , Spring 1951) These stories are collected in The Averoigne Archives: The Complete Averoigne Tales of Clark Ashton Smith , an ebook published by Pickman's Press in 2019. Geography Smith places Averoigne near the center of France, in the highland region known as the Central Massif. The northern half of the territory is dominated by the walled city of Vyônes , site of an impressive cathedral. In the southern half is located the town of Ximes. The main road of Averoigne runs between Ximes and Vyônes, straight through the thick, dark forest that blankets the province.

[1] Тьма (Darkness) L69 [Мифологическое описание]
The phrase "Lord of All Things" suggests Azathoth's supremacy among all deities. The impression is reinforced in the sonnet Azathoth , which refers to him as Lord of All [ Fungi online text ) XXII]. The sonnet also refers to "a cracked flute clutched in a monstrous paw, / Whence flow the aimless waves whose chance combining / Gives each frail cosmos its eternal law." It is not clear who is playing the flute; in conjunction with Blake's statement that Azathoth is "lulled" by a flute, it seems possible that some other entity plays the flute, and so influences Azathoth's dreams; thus "Here the Lord of All in darkness muttered / Things he had dreamed but could not understand." Azathoth's dreams perhaps then give rise to the various universes. On this theory, Nyarlathotep could be the puppet master who is really running the show, since he shows contempt for Azathoth: "'I am His Messenger,' the daemon said, / As in contempt he struck his Master's head." Another interpretation would be that Azathoth dreams while playing the flute himself, and the flute causes his dreams to come to life in the form of various universes.

[1] Йог-Сотот (The Gate) L45 [Энциклопедическая статья]
НАЗВАНИЕ: Basalt Pillars of the West ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:12:22 СИМВОЛОВ: 1068 Basalt Pillars of the West Location The Dreamlands Type Gate First appearance HPL The White Ship Appearances HPL The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath Created by H. P. Lovecraft The Basalt Pillars of the West are a pair of pillars of gargantuan size made of basalt (a dark volcanic rock) that rise from the ocean in the Dreamlands on the western edge of the world. The pillars form the gate of a monstrous cataract whose swift, resistless waters spill over the edge into the "abysmal nothingness" of planetary space. The pillars are shrouded in mist so that none may see beyond them until one sails through the pillars and the mists are lifted, at which point the current becomes too strong to escape. ( HPL The White Ship HPL The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath Basil Elton sailed through the Basalt Pillars aboard the White Ship on his search for the fabled land of Cathuria but never found it.

The temples of the goddess were located in Bubastis and Elephantine. Cat-headed Bubastis frowns down as a sullen guardian in the purple pylons before the pyramids. The ghost of Bubastis lurks in desert ways. Myths of animal-headed deities such as Bast are allegories of forgotten truths. 6] For Egyptian gods and religions were based on secret realities. Strange hybrids walked the earth when it was young; gigantic, lumbering creatures—half-beast, half-human. The priests of Bubastis viewed their god as a representative of monstrous beast-men who shambled on Earth in primal days. They regarded Bast as carnivorous, as the ghoul-goddess, Chewer of Corpses. Prinn's Saracenic Rituals chapter records that the priests were blaspheming against the reigning religions and performing atrocious sacrifices. The beast-mouths of the gods hungered for blood. The priests had made strange and curious bargains with their divine Masters. The priests were mating animals and humans in an attempt to create a hybrid with the attributes of their deity. Unnatural perversions drove the cult of Bubastis out of Egypt. After Nephren-Ka , the new ruler and his people drove out the wicked priests who prostituted their faith to carnivorous Bubastis.

НАЗВАНИЕ: Bhutan ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:12:31 СИМВОЛОВ: 981 Kingdom of Bhutan Location South Asia Type Country The Kingdom of Bhutan is a mountainous landlocked country in South Asia, bordered by China to the north and India to the south . The Call of Cthulhu Roleplaying Game In Chaosium Call of Cthulhu "Eyes Between the Worlds" scenario, Bhutan is home to a long-lost temple which houses the obscure Outer God Aiueb Gnshal and its cult of ghoul worshippers. The CthulhuPunk Roleplaying Game In the Steve Jackson Games tabletop roleplaying game CthulhuPunk , Bhutan has been incorporated into the Chinese bloc as one of its satellite states, primarily to provide a buffer for China against its political and military opponents.

Now under Yog-Sothoth's power and influence, Billy beat up Grim and stole his Scythe, using it to open up the portal in his basement, transforming his house into an eldritch location in the process. Teaming up with Hoss Delgado, Grim and Mandy find out that the only way to close the portal is to throw The Bad Book into it. After Billy swallowed the book, Mandy pushed him into the portal, ending the threat of Yog-Sothoth.

FILE: Billington House (Cthulhu Universalis).txt
Mentions: 2/2 | d:5.08/10k

[1] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L59 [Мифологическое описание]
In between the house and the tower is a marsh with frogs and whippoorwills that signal when the servants of the Great Old Ones (3) are present. In 1921, family descendant Ambrose Dewart decided to move into the old house and restore it. Stephen Bates visited him there later. Dr. Seneca Lapham inferred that an influence was being exercised on the inhabitants of Billington House. With the help of Winfield Phillips , Dr. Lapham was able to kill Richard Billington (who had possessed the body of Ambrose Dewart) and Quamis before they could finish summoning Yog-Sothoth into our world via a ritual at the stone tower. The location of Billington House is a bit difficult to visualize. The opening paragraphs of AWD Lurker seem to give the impression that Billington House is a short distance off the Aylesbury Pike as you proceed northwest from Arkham in the direction of Dunwich . From this, you might expect Dunwich to be somewhere to the northwest of Billington House. However, Laban Billington , when he lived at Billington House, heard cries "east by northeast, which is the direction of Dunwich, or the wild country around Dunwich."

[2] Тьма (Darkness) L117 [Мифологическое описание]
Billington House seems to be close to Arkham, which is odd since it is also close to Dunwich. Thus, "Squire Billington . . . made application to be heard by the Court of the County in its session at Arkham . . ." This suggests that Billington was living in the same county as Arkham, Essex County . Similarly, when Ambrose Dewart looked through old newspapers for information about Alijah Billington , he consulted only the Arkham Advertiser and Arkham Gazette , as if these were the most local newspapers. And John Druven reported talking a walking journey west and northwest of Arkham, and getting caught by darkness in the region of Billington's Wood, not far from Billington House; thus, we are either within a day's walk of Arkham, or Druven undertook a walking trip of multiple days. Also, when Stephen Bates was staying with Ambrose Dewart at Billington House and it was almost luncheon time, Bates suggested taking an impromptu trip into Arkham for lunch, as if Arkham was close enough for an impulse trip without unduly delaying their meal. With the help of Winfield Phillips, Dr. Lapham was able to kill Richard Billington (who had possessed the body of Ambrose Dewart) and Quamis before they could finish summoning Yog-Sothoth into our world via a ritual at the stone tower. The location of Billington House is a bit difficult to visualize. The opening paragraphs of AWD Lurker seem to give the impression that Billington House is a short distance off the Aylesbury Pike as you proceed northwest from Arkham in the direction of Dunwich. [2] Тьма (Darkness) L39 [Мифологическое описание]
Billington House seems to be close to Arkham, which is odd since it is also close to Dunwich. Thus, "Squire Billington . . . made application to be heard by the Court of the County in its session at Arkham . . ." This suggests that Billington was living in the same county as Arkham, Essex County. Similarly, when Ambrose Dewart looked through old newspapers for information about Alijah Billington, he consulted only the Arkham Advertiser and Arkham Gazette, as if these were the most local newspapers. And John Druven reported talking a walking journey west and northwest of Arkham, and getting caught by darkness in the region of Billington's Wood, not far from Billington House; thus, we are either within a day's walk of Arkham, or Druven undertook a walking trip of multiple days. Also, when Stephen Bates was staying with Ambrose Dewart at Billington House and it was almost luncheon time, Bates suggested taking an impromptu trip into Arkham for lunch, as if Arkham was close enough for an impulse trip without unduly delaying their meal.

He is engaged in unspecified "studying," largely nocturnal, because "he was better able to concentrate at night." He professes to "believe in ghosts and fairies, in ghouls and genies , in a certain mythological ‘prop’ [i. e. , the Necronomicon ], and in the existence of Atlantis R’lyeh , and G’harne ." Physically, he is described as tall and broad-shouldered and it was plain to see that in his younger days he had been a handsome man. Now, though, his hair had greyed and his eyes, though they were still bright and observant, bore the imprint of many a year spent exploring—and often, I guessed, discovering—along rarely trodden paths of mysterious and obscure learning. It is notable to this wiki for two of the five stories contained within; the first being an original Cthulhu Mythos story, and the second introducing a character who would later be incorporated into the Mythos. "Tales of the Zombie! : Damballah's Deeds" The story involves anti-hero Simon Garth, aka "The Zombie", tackling a pair of murderers in possession of a magic amulet which can control the dead. Among the Mythos elements made mention of are Von Juntz Yog , and R'lyeh Clarkashton and HPL are also both name-dropped. "Tomb of Dracula: The Blood Request" The entity known as Varnae lays the groundwork for Dracula to become the future Lord of the Vampires

НАЗВАНИЕ: Black Tallow ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:12:39 СИМВОЛОВ: 1265 Black Tallow Author Edward M. Erdelac Language English Genre(s) Horror Publisher April Moon Books Publication The Dark Rites of Cthulhu Publication date March 2014 Black Tallow " is a short Cthulhu Mythos story by American author Edward M. Erdelac Synopsis When Raymond, a specialist in translating ancient texts, is contacted by his old friend Paul, a successful businessman who wishes to pay him seven million dollars to translate a ritualistic text, he jumps at the chance. However, while translating the text at Paul's house, Raymond slowly comes to the realisation that in preparation for enacting the ritual - which he believes will allow him to commune with Yog-Sothoth and Azathoth amongst others, and grant him ultimate knowledge of the universe - Paul has murdered his wife and daughter, and rendered them down into tallow for devotional candles. In the meantime, Paul takes the translation but imperfectly completes the rite, and is consumed by an entity from beyond. Characters Raymond , a scholarly but poor man in his middle age. Paul Woodson , Raymond's former college roommate, now head of a successful multinational. "Black Tallow" was published in the Brian M. Sammons -edited anthology The Dark Rites of Cthulhu by April Moon Books in March 2014.

It was in January of 1914 that I next heard from him. Now in Peru, near Chimbote, Zebros claimed he was investigating the mountain worship of some of the northern Incas, apparently banned by the Great Inca, and supposedly destroyed by the conquistadors. Santiago claimed he had discovered this cult was alive and well in remote villages. I had heard such theories from Zebros himself, and wondered at the time if the old man was delusional. Таким образом я добрался до азотистого, поросшего плесневыми грибами портала семейного склепа. Примечания Примечания Симультанный (в психологии) (от лат. simul — в одно и то же время) — термин, означающий практическую одновременность протекания каких-либо психических процессов ввиду их свернутости и автоматизированности. Bran and his adventures take place in the shared universe of the Cthulhu Mythos as it was being developed by members of the Lovecraft Circle and H. P. Lovecraft himself. In the Howard-penned Bran story " Worms of the Earth ," explicit mention is made of black gods of R'lyeh , resting place of Cthulhu . In the earliest known draft of Worms , Cthulhu himself is mentioned but this was later changed to Nameless Gods in the final version. Also mentioned is Dagon Lovecraft in turn references "Bran" in his story The Whisperer in Darkness , which is interpreted by Clark Ashton Smith to be either Bran Mak Morn or possibly Brân the Blessed of Celtic mythology. Mythos Writing McNaughton's Mythos writing is characterized by black humor, considerable gore, and frank sexuality; "every character in [his] novels of any significance has a sexual identity and has thoughts and actions regarding sex and potential partners," critic Bobby Derie notes. H. P. Lovecraft The Dreams in the Witch-House When Walter Gilman managed to kill Mason, Jenkin replied in kind by burrowing though his chest and eating his heart. Brown Jenkin's bones were later found with those of Mason and several small children by workers tearing out a slanting wall. Behind the Mythos The origins of Brown Jenkin are subject to debate. Perhaps the most popular theory is that he is the child of Keziah and Nyarlathotep , the Lovecraftian deity she presumably serves. This is rather likely, considering that Lavinia Whateley mated with Yog-Sothoth , and that in The Lurker at the Threshold (posthumously published and co-written with August Derleth ) there is a quote that reads: "'She affirm'd, and her good neighbours likewise, that it had been borne to her, and took oath that she did not know by what manner it had come upon her, for it was neither Beast nor Man but like to a monstrous Bat with human face.'" Another theory, proposed by Weird Tales columnist Kenneth Hite , is that Brown Jenkin was a higher dimensional servitor of Nyarlathotep who was rewarded as being a familiar. However, as he was in the third dimension, he could only appear as a third-dimensional interpretation of what he was (this being similar to the vistas of Hyperspace in the story).

H. P. Lovecraft The Festival Byakhee are fictional creatures in the Cthulhu Mythos . They are predators who are known to travel in the vacuum of interstellar space. If one has the means by which to survive the myriad threats space presents, then one could ride a Byakhee to anywhere in the cosmos. When travelling beyond the speed of light, the creature's metabolism is greatly increased. When descending to the surface of any given planet, it is usually to feed, at which point it is best avoided. Overview This interstellar race is believed to serve Hastur the Unspeakable and may be summoned to partake in rituals. Composed of conventional matter, they are vulnerable to ordinary mundane weapons but possess cunning intelligence and guile, and some are able to cast spells. Dwelling in interstellar space, Byakhee do not have bases on Earth (although the Nameless City serves as a sort of harbour for them), but may be summoned to perform deeds or to serve as steeds, carrying riders through interstellar space - such riders may need to partake of the revered Space Mead to survive such cold journeys.

Senf Full Name Curtis Charles Senf Connection to the Mythos Artist Birth Date July 30, 1873 Birthplace Alsace-Lorraine, German Empire Death Date April 24, 1949 Deathplace Chicago, Illinois Nationality Prussia WT Curtis Charles Senf (1873 - 1949) was a Prussian-American artist who worked extensively for Weird Tales , regularly providing covers and interior art for the magazine from 1927 to 1932. During this period, he illustrated dozens of stories, including H. P. Lovecraft The Whisperer in Darkness Frank Belknap Long 's " The Hounds of Tindalos " and The Horror from the Hills Robert E. Howard 's " The Children of the Night ", and several tales by Clark Ashton Smith , among others. Senf's parents, Constantin Ernst Senf and Rosette "Rosa" Senf , moved to the United States in June 1881 with their four children. Senf was born in Alsace-Lorraine which had recently been added to the greater German Empire at the time. Senf and his family settled in Chicago and that is where Senf himself spent the balance of his life.

[1] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L31 [Мифологическое описание]
Huitzilopochtli was the patron god of the Aztecs who led them to the "promised land," the island in the center of Lake Tenochtitlan where they founded a capital, much as Yahweh led the Hebrews to Canaan. He has nothing to do with water or "Deep Ones" -- he seems primarily a war god -- again like Yahweh -- and he was born of a virgin-mother goddess. Perhaps the final letters of his name, "chtli," have something to do with Laney's correlation. At any rate, he would seem to be more likely one of the spawn of Yog-Sothoth, who is know to beget his progeny on mankind ... But in "The Mound" we read that the humans who occupy blue-litten K'n-yan, which land lies somewhere far within the earth beneath the southwestern United States, carried on trade or contact of some sort with the surface Indians of centuries ago. The people of K'n-yan worshipped Yig and Cthulhu, and their images often occupied the same temple. Furthermore, it is definitely stated that Yig is the prototype of the great Mesoamerican god Quetzalcoatl, the "feathered serpent."

His " Bells of Horror " (1939) is set in the fictional town of San Xavier, not far from Los Angeles. FILE: Call of Cthulhu, End Time.txt
Mentions: 2/2 | d:2.49/10k

[1] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L151 [Мифологическое описание]
Nyarlathotep : Is greatly pleased by what is happening on Earth and contributes to the insanity and madness. Rhan-Tegoth : It rules Alaska, where he is well fed by his cult. Shub-Niggurath : Her number of worshipers has greatly increased. Who make sacrifices to her regularly and are rewarded with fertile land and bountiful crops. Yig : It's power has been greatly increased and is attempting to re-establish the Serpent People as the overlords of Earth. Yog-Sothoth : Enters Earth often to feed upon its humans. Mythos Races Chthonians : Who visit the planet's surface more times than previously. Deep Ones : Have taken over many human cities and use the humans as both breeding stock and food. Many of the coastal regions have cities populated by both humans and Deep One/human hybrids. Dark Young : Roam across vast parts of Earth, searching for human prey. Dimensional Shamblers : Appear more often on Earth. Elder Things : A few remain on Earth, based in the ocean's deepest trenches.

[2] Гуль (Ghouls) L185 [Мифологическое описание]
Dark Young : Roam across vast parts of Earth, searching for human prey. Dimensional Shamblers : Appear more often on Earth. Elder Things : A few remain on Earth, based in the ocean's deepest trenches. They have formed an alliance with a group of humans. The descendants of naval personnel, who possess several warships and submarines. Fire Vampires : Who frequent the planet, where victims are gleefully chased by them. Flying Polyps : Have kept to their underground dominion. Ghouls : They have taken over various abandoned cities, where they have been feasting on the remains of the dead. Gnoph-keh : Much more active in the colder regions. Hunting Horrors : Which visit the Earth more often and enjoy hunting down humans. Mi-Go : Driven from Earth and the moon by the Great Old Ones. They still are very active in Pluto, have a small base on Mars, and perhaps elsewhere in the Solar System. Sand Dwellers : Little humanoids who are thriving in the deserts. Are building cities made of sand which are fused into a stone-like consistency.

Gameplay Gameplay involves two players, each in possession of a 60-card faction deck, who take turns playing cards in an effort to win rounds. Whoever wins the majority of three rounds wins the game. Decks may be preset ones found in the core set and various expansions, or built by players from cards permissible to their chosen faction. Core Set 2009, 165 cards. FILE: Canis Mysterium.txt
Mentions: 1/2 | d:7.17/10k

[1] Гуль (Ghoul) L89
This scenario is suitable as an introduction to a new campaign or can easily be worked into an established storyline. As written, this adventure is set in and near Arkham of October of 1930, making Chaosium's H. P. Lovecraft's Arkham supplement particularly helpful. Several scenario seeds are offered to keepers who wish to expand and continue the events in this adventure, perhaps giving birth to a new campaign or providing handy subplot sessions to pre-existing campaigns. Back cover text The storyline involves psychotic gravedigger Tobias Lurtz - heavily implied to have come from Ghoul stock - and his Ghoul companion as they attempt to use a forbidden text to raise an army of the dead and exact vengeance on the townsfolk of Coldwater Falls, who Lurtz believes have done him many grave injustices over the course of his life. Behind the Mythos Despite the back cover claiming that a copy of H. P. Lovecraft's Arkham would be helpful in running this scenario, Arkham plays no appreciable role in the story - the vast majority of the action taking place in Coldwater Falls, a town located some 60 miles from Arkham - and could easily be edited out entirely by the simple expediency of substituting a reason not involving Miskatonic University for the investigators to be pursuing a case in small town New England

In theory, it means a body of work that an established body of literature that can draw upon, but it is more commonly thought as what a fan considers what forms part of the Mythos, or what "really happened."

[2] Тьма (Darkness) L141 [Гримуар]
"Mythos Adjacent Works" include stories, films, et al that include elements lifted in part or in total from the Mythos, but were not by their creators intended to be a part of the Cthulhu Mythos. This would include works like the Hyborean Tales of Robert E. Howard, which share book titles and certain creatures, and the Army of Darkness film in which the Necronomicon is a central plot element. It also includes works that Lovecraft directly referenced in his works like Chambers' The King in Yellow. "Mythos Influenced Works" include stories, films, et al that include clear or subtle reference to Lovecraftian themes, creatures, etc.

[3] Йог-Сотот (The Key) L151 [Мифологическое описание]
This is to say, each main character/narrator (many of which assert their unreliability) is at best partially correct, and the information they acquire in the course of their uncanny experiences is of even lesser reliability. Lovecraft reminds us that we cannot understand the universe as it is, and perhaps gives us the key to the "harmony" of the Mythos: it is only discord. However, it is the opinion of most current Lovecraft scholars, and of this wiki, that the closer one comes to the original Lovecraft Myth Cycle, the closer to the "truth" one gets.

[4] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothothery) L167
There are discussion about what was intended as being part of the Mythos or not since he did not make a list for a collection publication while alive. In his letters,he referred to a story of this kind as a "Yog-Sothothery" and to refer to the whole as the "Arkham cycle" (specifically stating "The Colour out of Space" and "The Dunwich Horror" to be part of it). This terms are hard to use since the first would exclude stories which don't have the Great Elder themselves and the second one would exclude stories which don't take place in Arkham (such as "The Call of Cthulhu") but would include stories that could seem unrelated (such as "Herbert West--Reanimator").

[5] Тьма (Darkness) L247 [Мифологическое описание]

I cannot see a well or a subway entrance without shuddering . . . why cannot the doctors give me something to make me sleep, or truly calm my brain when it thunders? What I saw in the glow of flashlight after I shot the unspeakable straggling object was so simple that almost a minute elapsed before I understood and went delirious. The object was nauseous; a filthy whitish gorilla thing with sharp yellow fangs and matted fur. It was the ultimate product of mammalian degeneration; the frightful outcome of isolated spawning, multiplication, and cannibal nutrition above and below the ground; the embodiment of all the snarling and chaos and grinning fear that lurk behind life. It had looked at me as it died, and its eyes had the same odd quality that marked those other eyes which had stared at me underground and excited cloudy recollections.

FILE: Charles Fort.txt
Mentions: 1/1 | d:2.17/10k

[1] Тьма (Darkness) L41 [Гримуар]
Before terms like "UFO" and "cryptid" were coined, Fort's works dealt with the subject of extraterrestrial visitors and undiscovered animals, as well as psychic abilities, mysterious disappearances, meteorites with unusual properties, cases of animals or unidentified substances raining from the skies, etc. His influence was such that the word "Fortean" has become virtually synonymous with the unknown. In The Whisperer in Darkness , by H. P. Lovecraft , the main character Albert Wilmarth , initially skeptical about the existence of extraterrestrial creatures from local folklore , mentions how the defenders of such ideas have cited the books of Charles Fort as evidence to back up their claims.

FILE: Chorazos Cult.txt

[1] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L19 [Мифологическое описание]
НАЗВАНИЕ: Chorazos Cult ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:13:23 СИМВОЛОВ: 1332 The Chorazos Cult (erroneously called " Choronzon Cult ") is a religious cult dedicated to the worship of Yog-Sothoth . It appears in the Encyclopedia Cthulhiana , a supplement to the role-playing game Call of Cthulhu . The cult gets its name from the founder, a man of supposed gypsy descent who welcomed cultists from various parts of the world. This enigmatic and fanatical cult was founded in the mountains of Romania in the late 16th century, but moved to Elizabethan England. Although they owned a temple in Finchley with royal approval, an investigation by John Dee forced them to leave the place.

[2] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L33 [Мифологическое описание]
It was then that they settled in a house, but a year later the locals set it on fire, with which they cursed the place and left. It was then that Chorazos and his followers arrived in Scotland. Although King James IV opposed what he saw as witchcraft, the cult developed a good reputation due to its alleged healing powers, but was eventually disbanded again by the villagers as its true nature was revealed. The cult returned to the present day in the United States. Its goal is to awaken Yog-Sothoth. Curiosities The name of this fanatic cult could be an allusion to Choronzon, a demon that appears in the writings of the occultists John Dee and Edward Kelley, and that again would be referenced in those of Aleister Crowley.

НАЗВАНИЕ: Chthon ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:13:26 СИМВОЛОВ: 5489 Chthon Also known as The Great Shadow The God of Chaos He Who Sleeps The Demon of the Darkhold What Walked Once The Sleeper Beneath The Dark Majesty Who Has Slept Since Before Man Crawled From the Sea He Who Holds the Darkness The Sleeper What Dwells Beneath The Sleeping God The Dark Master The Other Keku Origin Earth Relatives Set (brother) Gaea (sister) Oshtur (sister) Affiliations Elder Gods (sometimes mentioned as part of the Great Old Ones First appearance EXP Marvel Chillers 1 (as "The Other") Avengers 186 (as Chthon) Created by Marv Wolfman, Yong Montano and Bill Mantlo Chthon is a fictional deity in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos . The character was created by Marvel Comics and made its first appearance in Marvel Chillers 1 (under the name "The Other"), but would not officially appear as Chthon until a few years later in Avengers 186. Since then, Chthon has been prominently featured as a antagonist throughout various story arcs, including the three-part story "Earth's Mightiest" in Mighty Avengers 21-23, where the readers get a true sense of his power for the first time.

НАЗВАНИЕ: Cimmeria ИСТОЧНИК: ROBERT E. HOWARD CIMMERIA — A POEM Cimmeria is a poem about the fictional country of Cimmeria where Conan was born in the Hyborian Age. According to Howard it was "Written in Mission, Texas, February 1932; suggested by the memory of the hill-country above Fredricksburg seen in a mist of winter rain." It was gloomy land that seemed to hold All winds and clouds and dreams that shun the sun, With bare boughs rattling in the lonesome winds, And the dark woodlands brooding over all, Not even lightened by the rare dim sun Which made squat shadows out of men; they called it Cimmeria, land of Darkness and deep Night. It was so long ago and far away I have forgotten the very name men called me. The axe and flint-tipped spear are like a dream, And hunts and wars are like shadows. I recall Only the stillness of that sombre land; The clouds that piled forever on the hills, The dimness of the everlasting woods. Cimmeria, land of Darkness and the Night.

Poetry: Until 1961 Smith published most of his volumes of poetry in this period, including the aforementioned The Star-Treader and Other Poems , as well as Odes and Sonnets (1918), Ebony and Crystal (1922) and Sandalwood (1925). His epic poem "The Hashish-Eater; Or, the Apocalypse of Evil" was written in 1920. Weird Fiction 1926—1935 Smith wrote most of his weird fiction and Cthulhu Mythos stories, possibly inspired by H. P. Lovecraft during this period. Creatures of his invention include Aforgomon Rlim Shaikorth Mordiggian Tsathoggua , the wizard Eibon , and various others. The stories form several cycles, called after the lands in which they are set: Averoigne Hyperborea Mars Poseidonis Xiccarph Zothique . Stories set in Zothique belong to the Dying Earth subgenre. His short stories originally appeared in the magazines Weird Tales Strange Tales Astounding Stories Stirring Science Stories and Wonder Stories . Many of the stories were published in six hardcover volumes by August Derleth under the Arkham House imprint. Some were also collected as Lost Worlds Vols 1 and 2 (LW1 and LW2).

[1] Йог-Сотот (The Key) L19 [Энциклопедическая статья]
Источник (URL): Название: Clavicle of Nyarlathotep (Cthulhu Universalis) Автор: Unknown Источник данных: live-сайт Символов: 706 Сохранено: 2026-08-25T21:58:32+03:00 SHA-256 контента: cae8615bc2602aa1c3decf0a2dc7417f16229c0d9d03cce79a1409ad14a7bd72 ТЕКСТ Clavicle of Nyarlathotep Georg Reuter Fischer heard voices mention the clavicle of Nyarlathotep as part of a list of books [FL Terror2]. In this case, "clavicle" is probably not a reference to a collarbone, but is used like the Latin word Clavicula, meaning a key. The title is reminiscent of the Key of Solomon (Latin: Clavicula Salomonis), a Renaissance-era book of magic that was misleadingly attributed to the Biblical King Solomon. One can surmise that the Clavicle of Nyarlathotep is a Renaissance-era book of spells that are attributed to Nyarlathotep. When originally issued, the book may have had a Latin title like Clavicula Niarlathotepus. Return to Cthulhu Universalis Contents Page

[1] Тьма (Darkness) L59 [Мифологическое описание]
on the bank of the Ton", with an "eldritch sign clumsily engraved on each wall", carvings that "were blurred by moss and weather." The town was once home to James Phipps, "a gaunt pallid-faced man, with jet-black hair, and long bony hands" who died in 1898, aged well over a century, and his son Lionel Phipps (1806-1931). Both were odd individuals given to "unorthodox scientific researches" and nocturnal excavation. They lived on Riverside Alley, "a little-tenanted street within sight of a bridge over the Ton". Outside of Clotton, according to "The Horror From the Bridge", there is a "pit on a patch of waste ground on what used to be Canning Road, near the river," containing "roughly-cut steps, each carrying a carven five-pointed sign, which led down into abysmal darkness." In " The Franklyn Paragraphs ", which mentions Clotton as a place visited by the cult led by Roland Franklyn , Franklyn's widow notes that "we went down the steps below Clotton."

НАЗВАНИЕ: Colin Wilson ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:13:53 СИМВОЛОВ: 2824 Colin Wilson Birth Date June 26, 1931 Birthplace Leicester, Leicestershire, England Death Date December 5, 2013 Deathplace St. Austell, Cornwall, England Nationality British Notable Works The Mind Parasites "The Return of the Lloigor" Spouses Betty Troop, Joy Stewart Colin Wilson (26 June 1931 — 5 December 2013) was an English writer who wrote fiction, including horror and science fiction, works on philosophy, especially philosophy in the Gurdjieff and Existentialist traditions, and nonfiction books on the occult. His novels included Lovecraftian elements, such as cosmic horror and impersonal if hostile entities from outer space. Writing in the 1970s, his works are also more overtly sexual and explicitly violent than those of earlier writers. Wilson's The Strength to Dream: Literature and the Imagination (1962) devoted a chapter to Lovecraft, "that man of dubious genius" who "carried on a lifelong guerrilla warfare against civilisation and materialism."

[2] Наг и Йеб (Lloigor) L77 [Мифологическое описание]
Challenged by August Derleth in the wake of this criticism to show that he could do it better, Wilson produced The Mind Parasites (1967), published by Arkham House , in which humanity is bedeviled by creatures called Tsathogguans . (In a preface, Wilson avers that Lovecraft, "far more than Hemingway or Faulkner, or even Kafka, is a symbol of the outsider-artist in the 20th century".) Wilson then wrote " The Return of the Lloigor ", first published in Tales of the Cthulhu Mythos (1969), which turned Derleth's minor Great Old One Lloigor into an alien species of psychic vampires --a depiction that has influenced subsequent writers, including Robert Anton Wilson, Alan Moore , and Grant Morrison Selected Bibliography Fiction The Mind Parasites (1967) The Philosopher's Stone (1969) (Reprinted, Valancourt Books, 2013) The Return of the Lloigor " (first published 1969 in the anthology Tales of the Cthulhu Mythos ; revised separate edition, Village Press, London, 1974). He traveled across much of the Hyperborian super continent from the Pictish lands in the west to Khitai in the east, from Hyperborea in the north to the Black Kingdoms in the south, and even discovering the Unknown Land (future Australia), and travelling to both coast of what would be known as the Americas. During his travels, he has encountered black sorcerers, hellish cults, ancient gods, demons, and eldritch horror several times, among them including a living idol of Tsathoggua Shuma-Gorath (lord of the Great Old Ones ), Sahb Delanzar (the Great Goat God, the God of a Thousand Young, seemingly Shub-Niggurath Yog-Sothoth (also known as Sodatha) and " Sodatha " (a monster believed to be Sodatha, and possibly a Great Old One itself), Azotharoth (possibly the Outer God Azathoth Thog the Ancient , and Satha (another name for Set ). Traveling to the Frozen Land ( South Pole ), he ended up in the Mountains of Madness, in Leng , where he saw the frozen corpse of an Elder Thing , and seemingly even destroyed a Shoggoth In one alternate reality , Conan tried to oppose a cult of fishmen and disciples of Dagon and save human captives (including a wench he had seduced), but was himself captured by Dagon himself and turned into one of his mindless worshipers.

FILE: Concerning Rudolf Hess, Mr Buckle and the Book.txt
Mentions: 1/1 | d:4.49/10k

[1] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L77 [Мифологическое описание]
Synopsis During the Second World War, James Worth, a highly skilled thief, is released early from prison by Mr. Buckle, a representative of the War Office, in exchange for the return of an item he stole from a British Museum storage warehouse: a copy of the infamous Necronomicon Worth soon comes to realise, however, that Mr. Buckle is not at all what he seems, and sets about the business of retrieving the cursed book. Tracking the man to a secret location deep beneath the streets of London, he thwarts a ritual to Yog-Sothoth being conducted by Buckle and his cronies. The group are seemingly destroyed by the Outer God in the city sewers. Behind the Mythos The Rudolph Hess mentioned in the story's title was a real-life German politician and deputy head of state during the pre-and early Second World War periods. He flew alone to Scotland with the intention of brokering a peace between his country and Great Britain, but was promptly arrested and held as a prisoner of war for the remainder of the conflict.

When she finally expired, he went to his mentor, Leffler, to give him the news. Leffler, despite his enviable knowledge about the Great Old Ones, Mi-Go, Deep Ones, and other creatures, was only a "theoretical" sorcerer, having given up the practice after an incident in which he summoned something that terrified and traumatised him. Price -edited fanzine Midnight Shambler Synopsis When a crazed vandal kills himself after defacing a company's icon - an enormous, rock-like sphere - head of security Colin James decides to look into the man's motives. What he discovers is that his city was once the site of a titanic battle, one in which Yog-Sothoth was rendered inert by cosmic powers. Furthermore, his company - which he now realises is far more expansive and insidious than he had ever imagined - is responsible for buying the land containing the inactive spheres of the Outer God , linking them together in an attempt to revive the being. The story concludes with James realising that even though there is little he can do against the forces ranged against mankind, he must try before the megacorporation achieves their goal.

[1] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L67 [Энциклопедическая статья]
It is unclear whether any of Lovecraft's fictional work meets both criteria. Questions center on who exactly owns or owned the , and whether the post-1928 — including such prominent pieces as At the Mountains of Madness — were renewed as required. Regardless of the legal disagreements surrounding Lovecraft's works, Lovecraft himself was extremely generous with his own works, and actively encouraged others to borrow ideas from his stories, particularly with regard to his Cthulhu Mythos . By "wide citation" he hoped to give his works an "air of verisimilitude", and actively encouraged other writers to reference his creations, such as the Necronomicon Cthulhu and Yog-Sothoth . After his death, many writers have contributed stories and enriched the shared mythology of the Cthulhu Mythos , as well as making numerous references to his work. The Open Cthulhu Mythos project relying on the extreme scholarship of the German Lovecraft Society have prepared a complete and exhaustive list of all Lovecraft works and elements that are beyond question in the public domain as of 2024 and after. A sign on a decaying warehouse reads Alhazred , a clear reference to Abdul Alhazred , the crazed author of the Necronomicon Adaptations An audiobook version of Nightmares & Dreamscapes was released with a reading of "Crouch End" by actor Tim Curry. The story was adapted into an episode of Nightmares and Dreamscapes: From the Stories of Stephen King by television network TNT. Trivia H.

FILE: Crypt of Cthulhu (Jack Ryan).txt
Mentions: 2/2 | d:16.82/10k

[1] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L51 [Мифологическое описание]
Consisting of four shorts connected by a wraparound story, it was independently published in October 2018. Both paperback and digital editions were released. Synopsis Dr. Gestalt, a supervising physician at Arkham Asylum , is mystified when four of his most promising patients suddenly slump into a catatonic state for no apparent reason. When the mysterious Dr. Ng arrives with a revolutionary device, the two delve into the patients' dreams, witnessing first hand their recurrent nightmares regarding the evil entities Cthulhu Dagon Yog-Sothoth , and Nyarlathotep At the story's conclusion it is revealed that Dr. Ng is in fact Nyarlathotep himself, and that accessing the minds of the comatose patients was a way to decipher the clues left by Cthulhu on how to awaken him and the other slumbering gods. Gestalt is able to thwart the Outer God's plans, but must sacrifice his own life to do so.

[2] Тьма (the Outer God) L57 [Мифологическое описание]
When the mysterious Dr. Ng arrives with a revolutionary device, the two delve into the patients' dreams, witnessing first hand their recurrent nightmares regarding the evil entities Cthulhu Dagon Yog-Sothoth , and Nyarlathotep At the story's conclusion it is revealed that Dr. Ng is in fact Nyarlathotep himself, and that accessing the minds of the comatose patients was a way to decipher the clues left by Cthulhu on how to awaken him and the other slumbering gods. Gestalt is able to thwart the Outer God's plans, but must sacrifice his own life to do so.

John Glasby EXP : "The Black Mirror" Cthugha (also known as The Living Flame ) is a fictional deity in the Cthulhu Mythos . Originally created by August Derleth , the character was first mentioned in his short story " The House on Curwen Street " (1943) but did not appear until " The Dweller in Darkness " (1944). Background Cthugha is one of the Great Old Ones that opposes the Elder Gods . As the elemental spirit of fire, Cthugha takes the form of a giant fireball located near Fomalhaut , who is served by the Flame Creatures . The entity can be summoned to Earth if the chant " Ph'nglui mglw'nafh Cthugha Fomalhaut n'gha-ghaa naf'l thagn! Iä! Cthugha! " is repeated three times when Fomalhaut appears over the horizon.

Background Cthugha is one of the Great Old Ones that opposes the Elder Gods . As the elemental spirit of fire, Cthugha takes the form of a giant fireball located near Fomalhaut , who is served by the Flame Creatures . The entity can be summoned to Earth if the chant " Ph'nglui mglw'nafh Cthugha Fomalhaut n'gha-ghaa naf'l thagn! Iä! Cthugha! " is repeated three times when Fomalhaut appears over the horizon. Cthugha appears as a demon lord in DC Comics' Arkham Asylum: Living Hell issue #6. Known as the "Arbiter of Hell", Cthugha takes the form of a squid-like entity who speaks in rhyme. [1] Йкнаггнсизсс (Zoth) L251 [Мифологическое описание]
Conversely, in The Transition of Titus Crow , it is strongly implied that the Cthulhi were already present on Earth when the moon was ripped off from the Pacific Ocean , taking some of their settlements. As the Cthulhi are known to affect the minds of other beings, their presence in the moon accounts for its historical association with insanity (as in the word "lunacy"), and is also the reason why dogs and wolves howl at the moon. Lin Carter, in his Xothic Legend Cycle , uses the term "Spawn of Cthulhu" to refer to the three sons of Cthulhu and Idh-yaa Ghatanothoa Ythogtha , and Zoth-Ommog . Carter rarely refers to the actual Cthulhi species in his fiction, although he does refer to them in the "Papyrus of the Dark Wisdom", revealing that, like the three sons mentioned above, the Cthulhi are also from Xoth. It's not known whether they are the children of Cthulhu and Idh-yaa as well. In the Worlds of H. P. Lovecraft comic book series, the "Spawn of Cthulhu" are actually the Deep Ones , and the white apes are merely an intermediary stage in the transformation of humans into Deep Ones.

Elder Gods and Great Old Ones A guide to August Derleth's changing terminology for the "good" and "evil" gods. The Cthulhu Mythos Derleth's understanding of the war between the gods, which led to the imprisonment of the evil gods and their continuing attempts to escape. The Elder Gods (1) An in-depth look at Derleth's benevolent gods: their origins, appearance, and abilities. The Great Old Ones (3) Derleth's concept of a single group of rebellious, evil gods, which conflates most of Lovecraft's pantheons of super aliens: the Other Gods , the Old Ones (2) of Yog-Sothoth, and the Great Old Ones (1) of Cthulhu. The Family Tree of the Gods The genealogies of the Elder Ones, according to charts drawn by H. P. Lovecraft and Clark Ashton Smith. Revised in 2024 with information about Ossadagowah. Guide to Arkham Arkham A complete guide to this history, features, and inhabitants of Lovecraft's signature town. Lovecraft's Map of Arkham HPL's hand-drawn map of one of his most famous creations. Guide to Dunwich Dunwich All the points of interest, amenities, local characters, and history of one of Lovecraft's most blighted backwaters.

FILE: Cthulhu Lives!.txt
Mentions: 1/2 | d:8/10k

[1] Тьма (Darkness) L53 [Мифологическое описание]
Overview At the time of his death in 1937, American horror writer H. P. Lovecraft was virtually unknown. The power of his stories was too great to contain, however. As the decades slipped by, his dark visions laid down roots in the collective imagination of mankind, and they grew strong. Now Cthulhu is a name known to many and, deep under the seas, Lovecraft's greatest creation becomes restless... This volume brings together seventeen masterful tales of cosmic horror inspired by Lovecraft's work. In his fiction, humanity is a tiny, accidental drop of light and life in the endless darkness of an uncaring universe -— a darkness populated by vast, utterly alien horrors. Our continued survival relies upon our utter obscurity, something that every fresh scientific wonder threatens to shatter. The dazzling stories in Cthulhu Lives! show the disastrous folly of our arrogance. We think ourselves the first masters of Earth , and the greatest, and we are very badly mistaken on both counts. Inside these covers, you'll find a lovingly-curated collection of terrors and nightmares, of catastrophic encounters to wither the body and blight the soul. We humans are inquisitive beings, and there are far worse rewards for curiosity than mere death.
