[1] Гуль (Ghouls) L29 [Мифологическое описание]
While distant oases shimmer and hover high in the desert air, the Sentinels stand with little thought, and even less, nay, with no care for the Wanderers. Yet they brood and they stare in the still days and the dark nights. They brood and they stare as the desert storms arise as upflung oceans of sand, shredding flesh and tearing internal organs from the Wanderers' sand-scoured bones, drowning nomads' tents, and sundering the walls of citadels and towns in its mindless noise and fury. They brood and they stare in the proper seasons when ghouls and ghostly forms and shrieking sand-demons rise and rejoice upon their pedestal of finely scoured stone. For the Sentinels live, but not as terrestrial beings do. They remember how and when they came here from the utterly cold and remote reaches of space. FILE: PSEUDOFACTUAL_MATERIAL_BY_THOMAS_V._POWERS_d80835af2a.txt
Mentions: 1/1 | d:0.48/10k

[1] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L39 [Мифологическое описание]
An argument can be made that certain aspects or occult practice were taken from the Elder religion, such as the ritual calendar specified in the Necronomicon. It has been speculated that the book was so secretly and surreptitiously circulated that even high church officials were forbidden to read it, if indeed they ever saw a copy, and were content to base their persecutions on local folklore and prejudices of the time. Ironically, the church seemed to have missed most of the few actual reoccurrences of this pantheistic religion (such as in Averoigne, France; where devotees of the Old One Yog-Sothoth are said to have made over one hundred human sacrifices during the 16th and 17th centuries), and instead concentrated on relatively harmless herbal healers, dimwitted practitioners of barely remembered fertility rites, and religious dissenters. In any case, it can be shown now that the worship of Cthulhu and the Elder Gods did exist, and it was extremely ancient and widespread. It is thought from study of anthropological evidence and from what few written records are preserved that widespread belief in the Elder pantheon died out over four thousand years ago in the old world, with the exception of a few shunned and isolated cults.

НАЗВАНИЕ: Pagan Publishing ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:26:50 СИМВОЛОВ: 2178 Pagan Publishing Parent Company Tynes Cowan Corporation Current Status Apparently defunct Founded Founder John Scott Tynes Country United States Headquarters Columbia, Missouri (1990-1994) Seattle, Washington (1994 onwards) Imprints Armitage House Pagan Publishing was a small publishing company whose focus was on Cthulhu Mythos games and related fiction. Overview Founded by John Scott Tynes in 1990 when he was just 19, Pagan Publishing's first product was the Call of Cthulhu fanzine The Unspeakable Oath . As the company grew and expanded it began to produce actual sourcebooks for the game, perhaps the most famous being the Delta Green supplement written by Tynes, Adam Scott Glancy and Dennis Detwiller Since it’s formation, Pagan Publishing has mostly produced content in book form, although it has also dabbled in the field of card games with Creatures & Cultists in 1993 and even released a modular board game in the form of The Hills Rise Wild! in 2000.

НАЗВАНИЕ: Pan (Cthulhu Universalis) ИСТОЧНИК: Pan "In ancient Greek religion and mythology, Pan is the god of the wild, shepherds and flocks, rustic music and impromptus, and companion of the nymphs . He has the hindquarters, legs, and horns of a goat, in the same manner as a faun or satyr . With his homeland in rustic Arcadia, he is also recognized as the god of fields, groves, wooded glens, and often affiliated with sex; because of this, Pan is connected to fertility and the season of spring." [ Pan , Wikipedia] Henry Armitage vaguely compared Pan to Yog-Sothoth when he said "Shew them Arthur Machen’s Great God Pan and they’ll think it a common Dunwich scandal!" [ HPL Dunwich online text )]. The analogy is to the storyline of Machen's story "The Great God Pan," in which Pan impregnates a human woman, who gives birth to an abominable child; just as Yog-Sothoth impregnated Lavinia Whateley , who gave birth to Wilbur Whateley and the Dunwich Horror Phillips Keith identified the Great God Pan as a synonym for Satan , the archetype of evil. Gazing at the creature, Keith experienced what the old priests of Pan used to call ecstasy.

Background Sekhmet was a high priestess of Ra in ancient Egypt whom was given the ability to turn into a panther and was worshiped as a minor deity. When Egypt was inflicted with famine and drought, bloodlust took over and she killed and devoured many, including her own son. For her crimes, she was condemned by Ra to walk the Earth for eternity. Lovecraft 's 1927 short story, also named " Pickman's Model Synopsis When struggling young artist Richard Upton Pickman meets enigmatic aristocrat Abigail Peters, he begins to develop an intellectual fascination with her, despite her apparent oddities. НАЗВАНИЕ: Pickman's Model Kit ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:27:00 СИМВОЛОВ: 913 Pickman's Model Kit Author Cliff Biggers Language English Publisher Ulthar Press Publication Pickman's Gallery Publication date Pickman's Model Kit " is a short Cthulhu Mythos story by author Cliff Biggers. It was published in the Matthew Carpenter -edited thematic anthology Pickman's Gallery by Ulthar Press in 2018. Synopsis When avid model kit collector Danny discovers a " Pickman's Model " kit of a ferocious ghoul in a run-down antiques shop, he is delighted, and snaps up the bargain, immediately rushing home to build his new prize. Over the next couple of days, strange disappearances in his neighbourhood, along with subtle changes to the model which suggest it reacts in sympathy to the events, horrify Danny, and he attempts to destroy the artefact. However, this only succeeds in summoning a real ghoul who appears to be somehow linked to the model, and Danny quickly becomes its latest victim.

[1] Гуль (Ghoul) L63
H. Vaughn. It was published in the Matthew Carpenter -edited anthology Pickman's Gallery by Ulthar Press in 2018. Synopsis The story charts the development of Richard Upton Pickman during his student days as a young artist railing against the stuffy, unchanging nature of the artistic community in the early 20th century, to the tempering of his work in order to gain acceptance by the local art patrons, and finally to realise what he needs to release his potential. At the same time it relates his relationships with two wildly different women, one the scion of a wealthy Boston family with a rebellious streak, the other a Ghoul working as entertainment in a disreputable speakeasy. Although both women provide him with inspiration for his work, in order to realise his true potential and become his muse, one must die at the hands of the other. Characters Richard Upton Pickman , a talented young artist who feels his work is directionless. Jane Channing , a young dilettante whose interest in Pickman leads to her gruesome demise. Althea , a stripper at a seedy nightclub, she uses a veil and strategically-placed feathers to hide her Ghoul nature.

Kiernan Publication Sirenia Digest Publication date October 2013 "Pickman’s Madonna" is a short story by Caitlin R. Kiernan that first appeared in the October 2013 issue of Sirenia Digest (#93). Overview The story introduces the characters of Isobel and Isaac Snow, albino, incestuous twins descended from ghouls , who raise an army to conquer the Dreamlands . The characters reappear in Kiernan's "The Peddler's Tale; or, Isobel's Revenge." The Snow family that they belong to is featured in Kiernan works like Low Red Moon and " Pickman's Other Model The story's title refers to an idol of a ghoulish goddess, first noted by humans in the 5th century, that was later in the possession of Richard Upton Pickman .

[1] Гуль (Ghouls) L71 [Мифологическое описание]
Contacting Pigman, he is lured into the depths of the New York subway system, where he is led to an abandoned rail cart and imprisoned. There, Pigman makes him the subject of his latest work, tattooing his entire body with horrific images before infecting him with an incurable strain of swine flu and depositing his near-lifeless body at an active station to infect more of the populace. Behind the Mythos Although never outright stated, Pigman and his inhuman clan are heavily implied to be Richard Upton Pickman and his pack of ghouls ; descriptions of his sublime yet shocking artistic talent, his first attack being launched in Boston , and the manner in which his acolytes' bodies move beneath their concealing clothes, all point in this direction. The city of Alaozar stood on the Isle of Stars in the Lake of Dread, hidden from common view by a barrier of trees (if they were trees). The gods Lloigor and Zhar are situated here. Sometimes called the Sung Region, the area is shunned by the non-Tcho-Tcho natives, and few men have penetrated the jungles to approach it. It is sometimes confused with the Plateau of Leng

FILE: Pnath [Abyss of Yhe.txt].txt

[1] Гуль (Ghouls) L79
P. Lovecraft Pnath is a region or city briefly mentioned as having been conquered by the city of Sarnath in " The Doom That Came to Sarnath " by H. P. Lovecraft . On the night of Sarnath's destruction, the king Nargis-Hei and his nobles were in the banquet hall of the royal palace, getting drunk on "ancient wine from the vaults of conquered Pnath". By the time of Randolph Carter 's visits to the Dreamlands, the vale of Pnath is a shunned area inhabited by the mysterious dholes . The floor is covered by half-eaten bones, as the Ghouls of the waking world use Pnath as a dumping ground to cast away "the refuse of their feastings", thrown from the edge of a crag that looms over the vale. Nodens night-gaunt servants "flop unendingly in the dark betwixt the Vale of Pnath and the passes to the outer world". Any intruders found on Mt. Ngranek are captured by the night-gaunts and taken to the vale of Pnath to be left to their own devices. ( HPL The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath

[1] Безымянный Туман (The Unspeakable) L65 [Мифологическое описание]
The sketch was written by series producer Jack Laird, directed by Jerrold Freedman, and stars Carl Reiner as the titular ill-starred academic. Synopsis A professor of comparative religion gives a lecture on an ancient belief system centered around the Great Old Ones , who supposedly ruled the Earth before mankind. Far from taking the subject seriously, the professor repeatedly comments on how absurd and preposterous the cult of the Old Ones is, and makes several jokes about the deities. When a student points out that mentioning Hastur by name is a taboo, the lecturer dismisses his concerns and speaks the unspeakable's name aloud several more times. At this point, a storm brews in the summer sky outside. The professor grows visibly nervous, but tries to hide it while continuing to make jokes. Finally, he produces a rare copy of the forbidden Necronomicon that he got from Miskatonic University and starts reading it, casually dismissing the book's warning about the "ghastly consequences". The storm rages while the professor continues to read the book aloud, until he is finally transformed into a monstrous creature before the shocked eyes of his students. Behind the Mythos According to Prof.

Behind the Mythos According to Prof. Peabody, the Great Old Ones include Nyarlathotep 'Umr at-Tawil , Hastur, Cthulhu Azathoth Shub-Niggurath , and Yog-Sothoth . He mentions that their cult has been active as recently as 50 years ago in Arkham , Massachusetts. The three students who ask questions during the lecture are named Mr. Bloch, Mr. Derleth, and Mr. Lovecraft, after seminal Mythos contributors Robert Bloch August Derleth and H. P. Lovecraft . Fittingly, Mr. Derleth is the one who points out that Hastur's name should not be spoken, as it was the real Derleth who came up with the deity's epithet "the Unspeakable". Also fittingly, Mr. Lovecraft is the one who asks questions about the Necronomicon , as the grimoire was Lovecraft's creation in real life. The end credits reveal that another student is named Miss Heald, after Lovecraft's frequent collaborator Hazel Heald Trivia "Professor Peabody's Last Lecture" was the only original Mythos story featured in Night Gallery , but not the only Mythos story overall, as the series also featured adaptations of " Cool Air Pickman's Model " and " The Return of the Sorcerer

FILE: Providence (comic book).txt

[1] Йог-Сотот (The Key) L93 [Мифологическое описание]
It is set in the same continuity as the " The Courtyard " and the 4-issue Neonomicon series, both also written by Moore. The premise of Providence is that Lovecraft 's stories are loosely based on the experiences of Robert Black, a queer Jewish journalist who is exploring New England in hopes of garnering material for a novel based on occult outsiders. This conceit allows Moore to rework Lovecraft's familiar fictions in his own unique style. Quest for Kadath See: The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath Revelation and Transformation See: Through the Gates of the Silver Key After obtaining the Silver Key , Carter performed the ritual of the Key in the hills behind Arkham, in the cave known as the Snake Den, on October 7, 1928. FILE: Red Star, Yellow Sign.txt

[1] Наг и Йеб (Lloigor) L57 [Ритуал и призывание]
It was published in the thematic anthology Historical Lovecraft by Innsmouth Free Press in April 2011. Synopsis In the aftermath of the unexplained assassination of a senior Soviet politician, man named Yezhov is tasked with uncovering the motive for this attack on the State. He soon uncovers a plot by mystical forces to interfere in the affairs of humankind and, after discovering the entity controlling the human assassin - a monstrous Lloigor - embarks on a course of action which he believes will result in the purging of all supernatural elements from his country. The story is interspersed with a series of missives between R'lyeh and the Leningrad Operational Center. These reveal that the initial assassination attempt was the result of poorly-planned meddling in human affairs; the final one explains how the manipulation of Yezhov and the sacrifice of a Lloigor agent had resulted in a violent program which would keep the secrets of the supernatural puppet masters safe for centuries.

[2] Наг и Йеб (Lloigor) L65 [Мифологическое описание]
He soon uncovers a plot by mystical forces to interfere in the affairs of humankind and, after discovering the entity controlling the human assassin - a monstrous Lloigor - embarks on a course of action which he believes will result in the purging of all supernatural elements from his country. Behind the Mythos During the course of his investigations, Yezhov discovers a small statue in the apartment of the assassin which he describes as looking like " a bat-winged man with staring eyes and a beard of squidlike tentacles ." This is a clear nod to the statuette recovered during Inspector Legrasse 's 1907 raid of the Cthulhu Cult , and ties in with the R'lyeh communications which exposit the antagonist's motivations in "Red Star, Yellow Sign."

[3] Наг и Йеб (Lloigor) L83 [Мифологическое описание]
Behind the Mythos During the course of his investigations, Yezhov discovers a small statue in the apartment of the assassin which he describes as looking like " a bat-winged man with staring eyes and a beard of squidlike tentacles ." This is a clear nod to the statuette recovered during Inspector Legrasse 's 1907 raid of the Cthulhu Cult , and ties in with the R'lyeh communications which exposit the antagonist's motivations in "Red Star, Yellow Sign." Although the entity encountered by Yezhov is named as a Lloigor, it bears no resemblance to the more commonly depicted members of that species, being described as having "vast eyes like glowing saucers, surrounded by a mass of squirming tentacles patterned in colours that shifted and shimmered," a much more generic Cthulhu Mythos description than its reptilian namesake. The Yellow Sign mentioned in the title refered to symbols etched on the statue found by Yezhov and imprinted on sewer walls by the Lloigor. Usually associated with the Great Old One Hastur , in this story the Sign was tied to Hastur's half-brother Cthulhu , the two entities being more commonly depicted as antagonistic in later Mythos stories. Trivia The assassination of Sergei Kirov was a real-world event which occurred in the Soviet Union in December 1934.

[4] Наг и Йеб (Lloigor) L89
Although the entity encountered by Yezhov is named as a Lloigor, it bears no resemblance to the more commonly depicted members of that species, being described as having "vast eyes like glowing saucers, surrounded by a mass of squirming tentacles patterned in colours that shifted and shimmered," a much more generic Cthulhu Mythos description than its reptilian namesake. The Yellow Sign mentioned in the title refered to symbols etched on the statue found by Yezhov and imprinted on sewer walls by the Lloigor. Usually associated with the Great Old One Hastur , in this story the Sign was tied to Hastur's half-brother Cthulhu , the two entities being more commonly depicted as antagonistic in later Mythos stories. Trivia The assassination of Sergei Kirov was a real-world event which occurred in the Soviet Union in December 1934. The killing would cause the already-paranoid state leader Joseph Stalin to initiate the Great Purge, a political cleansing which would result in the deaths of hundreds of thousands.

Cthulhu roleplaying game. Written by Scott Carter and John Houlihan , it was published by Modiphius Entertainment in 2023. Overview Welcome to Section M: Priority Missions, smaller one-shot missions and scenarios to help out the hard-pressed GM. Inside this PDF you’ll find a complete mission brief and full colour map to help you run a shorter one-shot session, plus a set of Adventure Seeds to provide inspiration for further adventures. In Resurrection Men Allied intelligence has discovered a network of Great War era tunnels near an impending advance. Section M has detected signs of a ghoul colony. Agents are to infiltrate the area in advance of the Allied movement, investigate the site to validate intelligence, and if necessary neutralise the colony as a potential threat. If the ghouls are not hostile, Section M is willing to let them remain in situ rather than risk agents or actions that might draw enemy attention to the area. If they cannot be persuaded to remain neutral, agents can use their discretion to ensure they do not represent a threat.

Rhan-Tegoth's victims are crushed and flattened, seared as if with acid, and covered with innumerable circular wounds. P. Lovecraft Richard Upton Pickman is a fictional character created by H. P. Lovecraft for his short story " Pickman's Model ". He was a renowned Boston painter notorious for his graphic works. Biography Lovecraft's Work Pickman's origins are ambiguous. His artwork depicts the ghouls as having the habit of abducting human children and replacing them with "changelings": ghoul children that look deceptively human-like, left to be raised by humans. One of the children depicted bears an uncanny resemblance to Pickman himself, hinting that he might have been one of those changelings.

He also contributed to Chaosium 's out of print Stormbringer and Elric! game lines, as well as to White Wolf's World of Darkness games in the 1990s. FILE: Russell's Guide to Interdimensional Entities.txt
Mentions: 1/2 | d:7.76/10k

[1] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L95 [Мифологическое описание]
The book focuses on body and alien horror through the lense of B. A. Lee's own Cthulhu -inspired work and mythos, Merrow Tales (2012). Specificities Canon modifications Most entries and descriptions are based on B. A. Lee's own work, Merrow Tales (2012). The bestiary's chapters also follow Lee's personal classification of beings and artifacts into five categories: Great Old Ones , Ascendency, Merrow, Star Spawn, and Subdimensional Entities. The book offers new names for several entities such as the Dunwich Horror (called Dumgal Zi Yog-Sothoth, "Prince of Yog-Sothoth"), Shoggoth (called Gugalushargal, "All Devourer"), Flying Polyp (called Bydogalzul, "Great womb of evil"), Mi-Go (called Star Spawn Drones), and so on. While each entry differentiates between entities sourced from H. P. Lovecraft or Lee's work, it points to Lovecraft as the sole source for entries that offer modifications to the canon. Psionic Alphabet Both Lee and Russell use a fictional alphabet named "psionic alphabet" in illustrations and occasionally in the text, mostly as a depiction of "true names". The alphabet is a phonetic collection of characters directly linked to English letters and diphtongs. Each letter, regardless of its use and placement in a word, possesses individual variations resembling small tentacles.

FILE: Saaitii.txt
Mentions: 1/1 | d:6.84/10k

[1] Тьма (Darkness) L63 [Мифологическое описание]
Later, In the Second Edition of Malleus Monstrorum , Saaitii is described as either Lesser Old One or Unique Entity. In the original Carnacki stories, the word "Saiitii" (sometimes spelled "Saaitii") is not the name of a single entity, but rather a dangerous class of supernatural manifestations, of which the titular monster from "The Hog" is identified as one. The word first appears in "The House Among the Laurels", and is also used in "The Whistling Room" and "The Hog". Background Saaitii is a minor Great Old One that resides in an outer realm, full of darkness and labyrinth tunnels. It manifests as a nightmarish swine, with rhino-like flesh covering its bloated, cadaverous form. Which has a tiny cyclopean eye, at least a dozen cloven-hoofed legs, and three maws filled with boar-like teeth and tusks. Saaitii attacks the souls of its victims, first possessing them and then dragging them into its lair where they are devoured.

FILE: Sabaoth (Cthulhu Universalis).txt
Mentions: 3/4 | d:18.24/10k

[1] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L29 [Художественный сюжет]
It is only in transliteration into Roman characters that they appear related . . . Joseph Curwen used the word "Sabaoth" to refer to some sort of mystic spell or incantation. He wrote that he " Say’d ye SABAOTH thrice last Nighte but None appear’d. " On another occasion, he wrote " Saw olde V. saye ye Sabaoth and learnt ye Way." The next sentence is " Rais’d Yog-Sothoth thrice and was ye nexte Day deliver’d. " So it is possible that the Sabaoth spell is for raising Yog-Sothoth . This spell may be the same spell that Charles Dexter Ward used when reviving Curwen, since that spell includes the phrase "Adonai Sabaoth," meaning " Lord of Hosts ." The spell reads: Per Adonai Eloim, Adonai Jehova, Adonai Sabaoth, Metraton On Agla Mathon, verbum pythonicum, mysterium salamandrae, conventus sylvorum, antra gnomorum, daemonia Coeli Gad, Almousin, Gibor, Jehosua, Evam, Zariatnatmik, veni, veni, veni. The same spell was used by Curwen to defend himself from Marinus Willett .

[2] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L63 [Мифологическое описание]
" So it is possible that the Sabaoth spell is for raising Yog-Sothoth . The same spell was used by Curwen to defend himself from Marinus Willett . Probably the spell is used to summon an entity such as Yog-Sothoth, who can then be further instructed to perform your bidding. Wilbur also mentions "He that came with the Aklo Sabaoth," which confirms that Wilbur used the spell to summon some kind of entity, possibly Yog-Sothoth.

This information was kindly supplied me by Eric Friedman, who goes on to state: "In the original Hebrew, it bears no relationship whatsoever to the word SABBATH (SHABAT), meaning 'rest'. It is only in transliteration into Roman characters that they appear related . . . " Joseph Curwen used the word "Sabaoth" to refer to some sort of mystic spell or incantation. He wrote that he "Say’d ye SABAOTH thrice last Nighte but None appear’d." On another occasion, he wrote "Saw olde V. saye ye Sabaoth and learnt ye Way." The next sentence is "Rais’d Yog-Sothoth thrice and was ye nexte Day deliver’d." So it is possible that the Sabaoth spell is for raising Yog-Sothoth. This spell may be the same spell that Charles Dexter Ward used when reviving Curwen, since that spell includes the phrase "Adonai Sabaoth," meaning "Lord of Hosts." The spell reads: Per Adonai Eloim, Adonai Jehova, Adonai Sabaoth, Metraton On Agla Mathon, verbum pythonicum, mysterium salamandrae, conventus sylvorum, antra gnomorum, daemonia Coeli Gad, Almousin, Gibor, Jehosua, Evam, Zariatnatmik, veni, veni, veni. The same spell was used by Curwen to defend himself from Marinus Willett.

FILE: San Francisco.txt
Mentions: 1/1 | d:2.9/10k

[1] Тьма (Darkness) L143 [Мифологическое описание]
Other Mythos Writers The Hunters from Beyond " (1932), by Clark Ashton Smith , takes place in San Francisco, featuring the fictional bookstore Toleman's and the studio of sculptor Cyprian Sincaul. The recurring character of occultist Michael Leigh , who appears in Henry Kuttner 's " The Salem Horror " (1937) and Kuttner and Robert Bloch 's " The Black Kiss " (1937), is based in San Francisco. Fritz Leiber 's 1977 novel Our Lady of Darkness provides a detailed portrait of San Francisco. Michael Shea 's " Copping Squid " (2009) taking the reader on a journey through San Francisco, "down Sixteenth through the Mission," "under the freeway and down to the Bayside, hanging south on Third," and up into the hills that overlook the city. San Francisco is also home to Shea's Hyperion Hotel , where he set a number of stories. In Ruthanna Emrys The Litany of Earth Innsmouth survivor Aphra Marsh tries to rebuild her life in San Francisco after being released from a government camp in Oklahoma.

[1] Тьма (Darkness) L75 [Художественный сюжет]
He has now returned to Chaosium in the role of senior consultant and advisor with input into design, game balance and syncretising the disparate elements of different Mythos writers into the standardised and statistics based approach of the Chaosium games. Prior to Call of Cthulhu Petersen worked long term on the rules for the RuneQuest games family as well as the Basic Role-Playing Game (BRG) universal rules, more recently released under an Open Games License (OGL). Petersen also designed the lion's share of the levels for the video games DOOM and DOOM II Petersen was the Executive Producer for the 2011 movie The Whisperer in Darkness which received award nominations at the Chicago International Film Festival and Warsaw International Film Festival (Foreign Feature division). The film was produced by the H. P. Lovecraft Historical Society Motion Pictures team in the style of a 1930s black and white horror movie.

Each person sees him in whichever aspect seems most natural to the beholder. An inverted pentagram represents represents Satan, Goat of the Sabbath. His followers believe that the Kingdom of Heaven is ruled by God, but that earth is ruled by Satan. If he grants them happiness here on earth, they are willing to forsake celestial joys. "They meet in hidden places—the cellars of ancient houses or ruined churches—on Walpurgis Eve and other unhallowed nights. Candles, fashioned from the corpse-fat of unbaptized infants, light their devotions to the Prince of Darkness. An unfrocked priest presides over the altar; the altar which is the naked, living flesh of a woman. All boast of their sins, and confess penitently their good deeds. Then, as the Lord’s Prayer is recited in reverse, a parody of the Mass is held. The Mass of St. Secaire, the unholy ritual of Gilles de Retz, and the Marquis de Sade. A sacrifice is given to Satan, and celebrants drink of a red wine which is truly human blood.

FILE: Satyr.txt
Mentions: 3/3 | d:8.43/10k

[1] Тьма (Darkness) L63 [Энциклопедическая статья]
P. Lovecraft Satyrs are imaginary creatures from Greek mythology, often depicted as having the upper half of a man and the lower half of a goat. Though creatures resembling them have frequently been incorporated into Cthulhu Mythos fiction, they aren't actual Satyrs in the sense of the Greek legends, but rather beings related somehow to Lovecraftian origins. In Lovecraft's Fiction In the story " The Horror at Red Hook H. P. Lovecraft describes a parade of horrific creatures led by Lilith in the catacombs below Red Hook, which includes "goat, satyr, and aegipan, incubus, succuba, and lemur, twisted toad and shapeless elemental, dog-faced howler and silent strutter in darkness". In Lovecraft's " The Nameless City ", the narrator's sight of the city's inhabitants evokes "comparisons as varied as the cat , the bulldog, the mythic Satyr, and the human being". In his " The Music of Erich Zann ", listening to the music of Zann --who is twice described as "satyr-like"--the narrator "could almost see shadowy satyrs and Bacchanals dancing and whirling insanely through seething abysses of clouds".

Price Language English Genre(s) Horror Science Fiction Publication Esoteric Order of Dagon APA Saucers from Yaddith " is a short story by Robert M. Price featuring Arwassa Overview In this story it is suggested that the Nug-Soth have visited Earth repeatedly from their homeworld of Yaddith to abduct humans and perform medical experiments upon the abductees. The experiments range from the swapping of a man's blood type from O to A to the swapping of eyes and hands to more nightmarish medical procedures. Obviously, this is a Mythos version of the Alien Abduction belief. "Saucers from Yaddith" was first published in the Esoteric Order of Dagon APA . It has since appeared in Etchings & Odysseys 5 (October 1984), The New Lovecraft Circle (1996), and Blasphemies & Revelations (November 2008).

[2] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L89 [Мифологическое описание]
Y. N. Freaks Haiyore! Nyaruko-san Fate/Grand Order The Scimitar of Barzai (also known as Barzai's Scimitar ) is a fictional artefact in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos . It was first mentioned in George Hay's anthology The Necronomicon: The Book of Dead Names , which describes the recipe for the item. It is named after Barzai the Wise from H. P. Lovecraft 's short story " The Other Gods "; however, it is unknown if the Scimitar has any connection to its namesake. Description According to the Necronomicon , the Scimitar of Barzai is a bronze scimitar that has the power to summon the Outer God Yog-Sothoth . In the day and hour of Mars, and when the Moon increases, the Scimitar should be made with a hilt of fine ebony, along with arcane symbols inscribed on each side of the blade. After the ritual is complete, the Scimitar must be wrapped in a cloth of black silk and set aside until it is used again. If anyone else tries to abuse the Scimitar's power, it will be rendered powerless.

[3] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L129 [Мифологическое описание]
After Tiberius summoned his Deus Machina known as Belzebuth, Kurou summoned a gigantic version of the Scimitar while piloting Demonbane. On an island near Innsmouth , Kurou used the Scimitar to fight off a pair of human-octopus hybrid monsters at the stone temple. Despite their regeneration capabilities, Kurou figured out how to defeat the monsters by surrounding them in a whirlwind of pages, using flames from the Scimitar to envelope the monsters in a whirling inferno. Later, during the final battle, the Demonbane trio used the Scimitar to trace Master Therion after they entered Yog-Sothoth's gate EXP Deus Machina Demonbane

Their diet consists mostly of fish, as well as the occasional lone swimmer. Unlike their land-based relatives, however, Sea Ghouls are cowardly creatures and thus never attack those who appear stronger than them, or who are part of a group. When they do attack, their strategy consists of savagely mauling their prey with their teeth and claws, while attempting to tear off oxygen tanks and other equipment, and holding down the victim until it drowns. FILE: Secrets of the Congo.txt
Mentions: 1/1 | d:4.07/10k

[1] Тьма (Darkness) L57 [Гримуар]
This is especially so in the still-wild regions of the Dark Continent, Africa. Darkest of all is the wilderness of Belgian Congo, in the very center of the continent. Belgian colonial rule is very harsh, and traditional practices such as slavery and witchcraft remain rampant. The few airmen who offer their services in such a place are veterans of the Great War. They navigate Central Africa by following the wide, dark, Congo River, but when night falls the only place to land is on the river itself. And there, in the African continent’s true heart of darkness, little has changed in the twenty years since Joseph Conrad wrote his well-known book on the hell-hole that is Belgian Congo. Superstitions rule the tribes that live on or near the river. The greed of the Belgian colonial administration, for ivory, rubber, and copper, surpasses even that of the Zanzibari slavers, feared for their raids among the Congo natives. This monograph consists of a series of linked adventures that bring the investigators on a flying expedition across the Atlantic and along the Congo River into the very heart of the Dark Continent.

P. Lovecraft The Servitors of the Outer Gods , also known as the Idiot Flute-players or Amorphous Flute-players , are a fictional species in the Cthulhu Mythos . They were first referred to by H. P. Lovecraft in his short story " The Rats in the Walls ", and are also featured in August Derleth 's stories, such as The Lurker at the Threshold The Servitors of the Outer Gods were later incorporated into Chaosium 's roleplaying game Call of Cthulhu EXP Malleus Monstrorum Background The Servitors of the Outer Gods are amorphous beings that resemble squids, frogs, and octopi which are constantly changing their shape and appearance. When needed they accompany the Outer Gods, though most of them are in the Court of Azathoth The music to which the Outer Gods dance to is made by these demonic drummers and flautists. On occasion they will also play for cultists to summon deities or to provide background music.

[3] Тьма (Darkness) L109 [Мифологическое описание]
When needed they accompany the Outer Gods, though most of them are in the Court of Azathoth The music to which the Outer Gods dance to is made by these demonic drummers and flautists. On occasion they will also play for cultists to summon deities or to provide background music. The "amorphous idiot flute-players" are often seen in the company of Nyarlathotep HPL The Rats in the Walls AWD The Dweller in Darkness One "amorphous flute-player" also played music to summon the Byakhee in an ancient Yule ritual partaken by the Crawling Ones HPL The Festival Behind the Mythos The Servitors of the Outer Gods share many similarities with the Moon-beasts from Lovecraft's novel The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath . The Moon-beasts are also amorphous, toad-like with squid-like tentacles, are often seen playing flutes, and are also servants of Nyarlathotep.

As for their origins, many servitor races are believed to have been created, spawned, or sired by their masters. For instance, the Tcho-Tcho people are said to have been born from "seeds" left by Zhar and Lloigor, and have since been trying to free their progenitors from the subterranean chambers where the Elder Gods have trapped them ( AWD The Lair of the Star-Spawn "). The Miri Nigri were given life by Chaugnar Faugn , who made them from the flesh of Earth animals. Unlike most other races, the Miri Nigri have no mind of their own, and live only to serve their creator.

The Shoggoths, meanwhile, are a rather unique case, in that they were created by the Elder Things ( HPL At the Mountains of Madness ) but chose instead to venerate and serve Ubbo-Sathla EXP The Descent into the Abyss In " Dreams in the House of Weir ", by Lin Carter, the Dholes are explicitly called Shub-Niggurath 's "servitors", while the Nug-Soth are only identified as her "worshipers", possibly implying a distinction. Despite venerating the same deity, these two species are blood enemies.

In the center of the plateau stood three stone towers joined by narrow catwalks of black metal between the roofs... At the top of the main tower is a dimensional gate to the planet Yuggoth Goatswood Main article: Goatswood Goatswood , first described in the short story " The Moon-Lens ", is an isolated town surrounded by woods to the east of Brichester. The narrator of that story is struck by the town's atmosphere: "The close-set dull-red roofs, the narrow streets, the encircling forests—all seemed somehow furtive." As in Lovecraft's Innsmouth , the residents of Goatswood have a distinctive, offputting appearance; a typical resident is described as "revoltingly goatlike".

[2] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L343 [Мифологическое описание]
Describing the town, the narrator notes that: around the blackened hotel at the center of Temphill, the buildings were often greatly dilapidated... gabled dwellings, often with broken windows, and patchily unpainted fronts, but still inhabited. Here scattered unkempt children stared resignedly from dusty front steps or played in pools of orange mud on a patch of wasted ground, while the older tenants sat in twilit rooms. The church of the title is set on a hill near the center of town, around which the town was built. It is said to exist "conterminously" with a temple of Yog-Sothoth . It is described: The steps... rose between green ruins of brick walls, to the black steeple of a church, among pallid gravestones... The tottering gravestones, overgrown with repulsively decaying vegetation, cast curious shadows over the fungus-strewn grass. Those who penetrate the catacombs beneath the church; reached via a trap door beneath the first set of pews; find themselves unaccountably unable to leave the town, as if the streets were turning back on themselves.

[3] Тьма (Darkness) L463 [Мифологическое описание]
The town's most noteworthy feature, also dating to 1931, is a "20-foot high concrete building... on the bank of the Ton", with an "eldritch sign clumsily engraved on each wall", carvings that "were blurred by moss and weather." The town was once home to James Phipps, who died in 1898, aged well over a century, and his son Lionel Phipps (1806-1931). Both were odd individuals given to "unorthodox scientific researches" and nocturnal excavation. They lived on Riverside Alley, "a little-tenanted street within sight of a bridge over the Ton". Outside of Clotton, according to "The Horror From the Bridge", there is a "pit on a patch of waste ground on what used to be Canning Road, near the river," containing "roughly-cut steps, each carrying a carven five-pointed sign, which led down into abysmal darkness." In " The Franklyn Paragraphs ", which mentions Clotton as another place visited by the Franklyn circle, Franklyn's widow notes that "we went down the steps below Clotton." Camside Main article: Camside Camside is home to the occultist Henry Fisher, who summons the Outer God Daoloth in the story " The Render of the Veils ". Fisher was expelled from Brichester University in " The Mine on Yuggoth ".

Turning to the Lovecraft's legacy, Derie discusses a number of writers in the Mythos tradition whose work has dealt with sexual themes to a greater or lesser extent, including Robert E. Howard Clark Ashton Smith Robert Bloch August Derleth Ramsey Campbell Richard A. Lupoff Peter H. Cannon Brian McNaughton Robert M. Price W. H. Pugmire Caitlín R. Kiernan , Edward Lee, and Alan Moore The book makes note of the magazine Cthulhu Sex (1998—2007) and anthologies of erotic Mythos fiction such as Eldritch Blue: Love & Sex in the Cthulhu Mythos (2004), Cthulhurotica (2010), and Whispers in Darkness: Lovecraftian Erotica (2011). While critical discussions of the Mythos generally focus on written fiction, Derie looks more broadly at the sexuality in the Lovecraftian occult, and in art, comics, and cinema.

[2] Йог-Сотот (the Late [fuzzy:88%]) L69 (fuzzy)

FILE: Shabbith-Ka.txt
Mentions: 1/2 | d:11.02/10k

[1] Безымянный Туман (The Unspeakable) L51 [Мифологическое описание]
НАЗВАНИЕ: Shabbith-Ka ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:28:22 СИМВОЛОВ: 1704 Shabbith-Ka Species Outer God First appearance EXP The Unspeakable Oath 8/9 Created by Jeff Moeller Shabbith-Ka is a Lesser Outer God which appears in the H. P. Lovecraft -inspired Cthulhu Mythos . Created by Jeff Moeller , it appeared in the Call of Cthulhu roleplaying game scenario "What Goes Around, Comes Around," first published in The Unspeakable Oath 8/9, and later included in the collection The Resurrected III: Out of the Vault Description Shabbith-Ka manifests as an amorphous blob of glowing purple energy; staring at the entity for long enough may allow the viewer to discern the outline of a rudimentary face, although what effect such an action might have on the person's sanity is enough to make one shudder. The entity's worshippers summon it through the use of a particular spell, which is employed in the form of a song. When summoned, anyone not under the protection of an Elder Sign or actively singing the summoning spell will be attacked and consumed by it. It achieves this by absorbing the person into its "body," leaving nothing behind but a purple-tinged husk, which quickly disintegrates into ashes. Due to the nature of its form, physical weapons are useless against Shabbith-Ka.

[3] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L83 [Мифологическое описание]
Overview The first scenario supplement for Call of Cthulhu Shadows of Yog-Sothoth contains a seven-part campaign and two stand-alone adventures. The campaign takes the players across the globe in pursuit of the cult of the Hermetic Order of the Silver Twilight , from America ’s east coast to Scotland to the South Pacific. The two adventures consist of "The People of the Monolith", a trip to Hungary in search of a mysterious poet, and "The Warren", the hunt for a missing friend in Boston. Released in 1982, the first edition of Shadows of Yog-Sothoth ran to 72 pages and featured artwork by Tom Sullivan . In 1989, it was collected along with other previously-published playing material and an all-new scenario in Cthulhu Classics , while in 2004, it was re-released in an updated format for the sixth edition of Call of Cthulhu along with new material and artwork. This version ran to 144 pages.

FILE: Shambler From the Stars (Cthulhu Universalis).txt
Mentions: 1/1 | d:6.27/10k

[1] Безымянный Туман (Magnum Innominandum) L17 [Ритуал и призывание]
НАЗВАНИЕ: Shambler From the Stars (Cthulhu Universalis) ИСТОЧНИК: Shambler From the Stars A familiar or servitor from beyond the stars that can be summoned with an orison or spell from De Vermis Mysteriis . The long and sinister invocation begins with " Tibi, Magnum Innominandum , signa stellarum nigrarum et bufoniformis Sadoquae sigillum.... " Per Google Translate , this apparently means something like "To thee, Great Nameless One, the signs of the black stars and the toad-shaped seal of Sadoqua ( Tsathoggua )". When a mystic dreamer in Providence read the spell aloud, the creature's arrival was heralded by extreme cold and the sound of cunning laughter. The creature was initially invisible when it lifted up the dreamer, tore his neck, and drank his blood.

[1] Безымянный Туман (Magnum Innominandum) L21 [Ритуал и призывание]
Источник (URL): Название: Shambler From the Stars (Cthulhu Universalis) Автор: Unknown Источник данных: live-сайт Символов: 1418 Сохранено: 2026-08-25T21:59:48+03:00 SHA-256 контента: 2f6b1a110e83f1f22e4da6af9f0675ad1fc595976332b295ba92df79f4da98d5 ТЕКСТ Shambler From the Stars A familiar or servitor from beyond the stars that can be summoned with an orison or spell from De Vermis Mysteriis. The long and sinister invocation begins with "Tibi, Magnum Innominandum, signa stellarum nigrarum et bufoniformis Sadoquae sigillum...." Per Google Translate, this apparently means something like "To thee, Great Nameless One, the signs of the black stars and the toad-shaped seal of Sadoqua (Tsathoggua)". When a mystic dreamer in Providence read the spell aloud, the creature's arrival was heralded by extreme cold and the sound of cunning laughter. The creature was initially invisible when it lifted up the dreamer, tore his neck, and drank his blood.

НАЗВАНИЕ: Shane Ivey ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:28:46 СИМВОЛОВ: 1064 Shane Ivey Connection to the Mythos Games designer Editor Nationality United States Genre Roleplaying games Shane Ivey is an American games designer whose output has included numerous contributions to Cthulhu Mythos works. His gaming credits include the core rulebook for the Delta Green stand-alone horror roleplaying game as well as a large number of its supplements, and several books for Cubicle 7 Entertainment 's Tolkenian fantasy The One Ring Roleplaying Game Ivey is also the co-founder, with Dennis Detwiller , of Arc Dream Publishing , through which they publish Delta Green and the resurrected roleplaying magazine The Unspeakable Oath , for which he is the editor-in-chief. He also worked for the now-defunct Pagan Publishing , several of whose works Ivey and Detwiller have continued through Arc Dream. Much of Appelcline's Mythos-related output was accomplished in supplements for Chaosium Call of Cthulhu horror roleplaying game. Appelcline's non-Mythos work includes writing for White Wolf Publishing, designers of the hugely popular World of Darkness setting. He is also the vice president of Skotos Tech, owners of the roleplaying game site RP Gnet, where is the editor-in-chief. [1] Тьма (Darkness) L41 [Энциклопедическая статья]
НАЗВАНИЕ: Sheila ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:28:46 СИМВОЛОВ: 2018 Sheila Also known as The Chosen One Sheila Williams Powers and Abilities Swordsmanship Melee Combat Proficiency Occupation Noblewoman Warrior S-Mart Clerk Teacher Species Human First appearance EXP Army of Darkness Created by Sam Raimi Sheila (also known as The Chosen One ) is a fictional hero created by Sam Raimi for the 1992 comedy-fantasy film Army of Darkness , the third installment of Raimi's Evil Dead franchise. Background Sheila was a maiden in 1300 AD who first hated the time displaced Ash Williams and then fell in love with him. A Deadite possessed her and she turned into "Bad Sheila". Upon the defeat of Evil Ash and the Army of Darkness, she was freed of the Deadite and witnessed Ash's return back home to his own time. Another version married Ash Williams who decided to stay in 1300 AD. This version had lost her right hand, and battled Deadites alongside her husband.

[2] Тьма (Darkness) L77
Background Sheila was a maiden in 1300 AD who first hated the time displaced Ash Williams and then fell in love with him. A Deadite possessed her and she turned into "Bad Sheila". Upon the defeat of Evil Ash and the Army of Darkness, she was freed of the Deadite and witnessed Ash's return back home to his own time. Another version married Ash Williams who decided to stay in 1300 AD. This version had lost her right hand, and battled Deadites alongside her husband. Pregnant with his child, they married. Unfortunately during the reception party, a drunken Ash spoke the words "Klaatu Barada Nikto" which sent him to 1350 AD. In another reality, after Ash returned to his time, she was convinced by the Wise Man and Lord Arthur to help them create a team to continue the teachings of the Promised One.

The Mound narrator compares Shub-Niggurath to a "sophisticated Astarte ." Astarte was an ancient Semitic goddess; the comparison suggests a cult of fertility, which is consistent with the epithet "All-Mother." Zamacona, a pious Catholic, found the rites of Shub-Niggurath to be repulsive, most especially the emotional sounds uttered by the celebrants.

[3] Йог-Сотот (Yog) L65 [Мифологическое описание]

[ HPL Mound online text )] According to Von Junzt's Nameless Cults , Shub-Niggurath was worshipped in ancient Mu as the Mother Goddess and the Goat with a Thousand Young. A copper temple was dedicated to her. T'yog , the High Priest of Shub-Niggurath, regarded her as one of the gods friendly to humanity, and felt inspired by her to try to vanquish the malignant cult of Ghatanothoa . T'yog also counted on the help of Shub-Niggurath's sons; these might perhaps be the deities Nug and Yeb , whom T'yog also regarded as friendly to man. [5] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L133 [Гримуар]
Random Invocations Devotees of arcane cults tend to call out to Shub-Niggurath whenever they get excited. There is a startling lack of continuity to these interjections, which often pop up in conversations or writings that otherwise seem unrelated to Shub-Niggurath. It is almost as if the phrase implies devotion and awe for all the elder deities, rather than merely Shub-Niggurath. Thus, In the midst of a Necronomicon passage describing Yog-Sothoth and the Old Ones (2) Alhazred wrote "Iä! Shub-Niggurath!" [ Dunwich online text )]. In his diary, Daniel Morris wrote the exclamation "Iä! Shub-Niggurath!" [ Man online text )]. Morris had a copy of the Book of Eibon , so perhaps he had read of Shub-Niggurath in that book.

[6] Тьма (Darkness) L399 [Мифологическое описание]
A similar passage from the R'lyeh Text refers to "his" thousand young [ Sky ]. Another Necronomicon passage refers to "his" hideousness [ Lurker ]. Earth Elemental Shub-Niggurath is one of the earth beings [ Dweller Island ] and dwells within the earth [ Curwen ]. Offspring Shub-Niggurath has hideous offspring that also dwell within the earth. [ Curwen And Nyarlathotep Upton Gardner speculated whether the Dweller in Darkness manifesting in the Wood of N'gai might be Shub-Niggurath; but it later became clear that this being was actually Nyarlathotep Dweller ]. Gardner's confusion may have arisen from the fact that Shub-Niggurath and Nyarlathotep are both earth beings. A similar confusion occurred when Marius Phillips interpreted Sylvan's notes as saying that Shub-Niggurath is the Messenger of the Gods [ Seal online text )].

[7] Йог-Сотот (Yog) L589 [Мифологическое описание]
Dan Harrop heard the name Shub-Niggurath in his mind [ Whippoorwills ]. Sylvan Phillips wrote of Shub-Niggurath in his notes [ Seal online text )]. Ward Phillips (1) wrote of Shub-Niggurath in his fictions [ Lamp online text )]. A worshipper in the Wood of N'gai called out to Shub-Niggurath [ Dweller ]. Other Sources The "bitch-goddess" Shub-Niggarauth arrived with Yog-Sototh and Yeb at a worship ceremony for the latter at Black Mountain. [ RHB Garoth Simon Maglore asked old farmers if they had heard of Shub-Niggurath [ RB Mannikin ]. Willie Osborne heard a buzzing voice chanting to "shub nigger" [ RB Notebook online text )]. Albert Keith dreamed of creatures worshipping Shub-Niggurath. Reverend Nye spoke of Shub-Niggurath to his congregation [ RB Strange ].

[1] Тьма (Darkness) L53 [Мифологическое описание]
Published by the First United Church of Cthulhu via CreateSpace in February 2016, it was created by Khurt Khave , the head priest of that organisation. Overview This magickal tome includes the English translations of H. P. Lovecraft 's works involving the praise and worship of Shub-Niggurath , including original versions in their native tongues: The Whisperer in Darkness in Malachim (whose variations include Angelic Script and the Celestial Alphabet), The Last Test in Arabic, The Mound in Sumerian/Akkadian cuneiform, Out of the Aeons in Phoenician/Moabite, The Thing on the Doorstep in runic inscription, and The Dreams in the Witch-House in the secret language of alchemic sigilry. A great resource for followers of Shub-Niggurath as it includes all the autochthonous manuscripts about The Black Goat of the Woods with a Thousand Young as transcribed by our mad prophet H. P. Lovecraft. Also a great learning tool for aspiring psychonauts and chaos mages. Can be utilized as a roleplaying accessory for the Call of Cthulhu RPG or any other horror or fantasy LARP that needs a Lovecraftian twist.

НАЗВАНИЕ: Shuggob ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:29:02 СИМВОЛОВ: 1227 Shuggob Origin Vale of Pnath Dreamlands Occupation Sorcerer Species Ghoul First appearance EXP In the Vale of Pnath Created by Lin Carter Shuggob is a fictional character created by Lin Carter for his Cthulhu Mythos short story " In the Vale of Pnath Description Shuggob is an elderly ghoul sage who lives alone in a stone house surrounded by a garden of moss and lichens, with a hedge made of mottled fungi, in the part of the Dreamlands known as the Vale of Pnath . He is extremely knowledgeable about magic and skilled in the craft of potions. Somewhat unusually for a ghoul, Shuggob is a soft-spoken individual of gentlemanly demeanor and scholarly inclinations. He is amicable and receptive to strangers, offering them food and drinks of the type generally consumed by his species, i. e. made from human flesh and blood. In terms of physical appearance, Shuggob is tall and lean. His skin is grey, cold to the touch, and rubbery, and his hands are surprisingly strong.

Y. N. Freaks The Silver Key is a fictional artefact in the Cthulhu Mythos . It was originally created by H. P. Lovecraft for his eponymous short story Overview The Silver Key is an ancient magical artefact that unlocks gates of space and time, allowing access to remote times and places of the universe. It was last in the possession of Randolph Carter , who used it to travel through the Ultimate Gate It is described as "a huge key of tarnished silver covered with cryptical arabesques". Carter has a vision of his late grandfather, who tells him where to find the key: It's in a box in the attic of his Boston home, where it was placed by Edmund Carter, his ancestor who lived at the time of the Witch Trials. The key had been handed down to Edmund by ancestors further back: Randolph's grandfather mentions Sir Randolph Carter, an Elizabethan wizard, and another ancestor who lived at the time of the Crusades and learned secrets from the Saracens who held him captive. Randolph Carter eventually uses the Silver Key to go back in time, reverting from his adult self in 1928 to his child self in 1883.

Behind the Mythos The Skinless One was designed by Geoff Gillan for the Call of Cthulhu campaign expansion Horror on the Orient Express . It was later included in the monster manual Ye Booke of Monstres II Based on the quotation included in Ye Booke of Monstres II , it would appear that the Skinless One was inspired by a passage from H. P. Lovecraft 's short story " The Whisperer in Darkness To Nyarlathotep, Mighty Messenger, must all things be told. and He shall put on the semblance of men, the waxen mask and the robe that hides, an come down from the world of the Seven Suns to mock. Penelope Love , another of the contributors to Horror on the Orient Express , used the Skinless One as an antagonist in her 2014 short story " Daddy, Daddy ," included in the tie-in anthology Madness on the Orient Express , released to coincide with the revised edition of the original campaign.

FILE: So Runs the World Away.txt
Mentions: 6/6 | d:12.21/10k

[1] Гуль (Ghouls) L69 [Гримуар]
Kiernan Country United States Language English Portuguese Publisher Robinson Publication The Mammoth Book of Vampire Stories by Women Publication date October 2001 "So Runs the World Away" is a short story by American author Caitlin R. Kiernan that introduces her setting of the supernatural underworld of Providence Rhode Island , which she used as the milieu for several subsequent stories. It was first published in 2001 in The Mammoth Book of Vampire Stories by Women . It was later reprinted in Kiernan's collection To Charles Fort, With Love , and in their 2018 Cthulhu Mythos omnibus Houses Under the Sea Overview The story focuses on an undead creature known as Dead Girl who seems to have trouble fitting in to the societies of ghouls and vampires who dominate the Providence dark world. She is preoccupied with remembering the human life she had before her transition, an impulse discouraged by the character known as The Bailiff: "We forget for a reason, child," he tells her. "Time is too heavy to carry so much of it strung about our necks." The story introduces characters and settings that will play important roles in later fiction by Kiernan, including The Bailiff, Madame Terpsichore, and the house on Benefit Street.

The Swan Point Cemetery has a mausoleum for the Stanton family where Dead Girl keeps a cigar box full of secrets.

The story also contains a description of Lovecraft's gravesite in the cemetery, as well as a nearby tree where fans have carved the "unpronounceable names of dark, fictitious gods and entire passages from Lovecraft," as well "a scar in the shape of a tentacle-headed fish, a parody of the Christian ichthus." Characters Dead Girl , an undead woman who sleeps at the bottom of the Sekonk River. (Brown was a real person who was actually accused of vampirism after her death.) Bobby , Dead Girl's companion. Too many CoC games ended with my investigator dead and the mystery unsolved. Apocthulhu is different. It takes place after the bad guys won. The cultists were right and possibly R'yleh [sic] has risen. We are then into a post-apocalyptic game but rather than zombies or a nuclear wasteland we are dealing with a mythos spawned apocalypse setting. Apocthulhu is derived from various OGL sources, such as Legend, and uses a very familiar d100, roll under your skill mechanic. One of the key features of the setting(s) is the scarcity of resources. The core oracle in these solo rules mimics the scavenging skill resolution and that carries on through to controlling NP Cs in your world, and for running published adventures. This solo set contains a page on safety tools, this may strike you as odd in solo play, but I felt that there was a place for them in this genre. Publishers description

[1] Йог-Сотот (The Gate) L123 [Энциклопедическая статья]
Trivia Many characters from "Cool Air" who were unnamed in the original story are identified by name for the first time in this retelling: Most notably, the "Cool Air" narrator is identified as Randolph Carter, a recurring character in Lovecraft's stories. Dr. Muñoz is given the first name Hector. The plumber whose arm was fixed by Muñoz is named O'Reilly, and identified as the same mechanic who was called later to fix the refrigerating unit. Mrs. Herrero's son is named Esteban. Bertie Wooster is shown to have some knowledge of the Dreamlands , mentioning Night-gaunts Zoogs , and the seven-hundred steps to the Gate of Deeper Slumber ( HPL The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath ). Either Wooster is a dreamer or he has learned about these things from his new friend Carter. When Wooster meets Mrs. Herrero, there is a humourous exchange in which she asks " Qué? " and Carter tells Wooster not to mind her because "she's from Barcelona". While Mrs. Herrero was indeed from Barcelona in the original story, this exchange is also a reference to a recurring routine involving the character Manuel (also from Barcelona) in the British comedy series Fawlty Towers

They were later incorperated into Chaosium 's role-playing game Call of Cthulhu EXP Ye Booke of Monstres Background The Spawn of the Green Abyss are a highly evolved and intelligent race which lives in the oceans and seas of Earth. Living in societies ruled by their queen, Zoth Syra. They appear as bluish slime whose various features are shifting. Limbs and sensory organs are created as needed. The songs of the spawn can influence those whom hear it. Though normal weapons cannot hurt them, they can be harmed by fire, chemicals, electricity, magical spells, and enchanted weapons. The Spawn of the Green Abyss herald from outer space and came to this planet long ago to inhabit oceans and watery places.

[2] Йкнаггнсизсс (Zoth) L73 [Мифологическое описание]
The Spawn of the Green Abyss herald from outer space and came to this planet long ago to inhabit oceans and watery places. While similar to the Shoggoths , in some respects, the spawn are utterly alien and possess great intelligence, sometimes traveling in groups for undecipherable reasons. They tend to remain in deep waters, occasionally swimming to the surface to hold what appear to be strange rituals when certain cosmic alignments take place. Some fishermen—who claimed to have been taken down into the depths by the spawn—speak of the monsters dwelling in bizarre aquatic societies and that they are ruled by beings named Zoth Syra and with Kala. Some have alleged the spawn are actually part of Deep One society and can be found deep within that race’s underwater cities. The spawn appears as a bluish-black slime with various and shifting features, able to create limbs and sensory organs as needed. They are capable of speech, including human tongue, and use a form of "singing" that, akin to old sea tales of mermaid and siren song, is able to command the will of weak-willed folk.

FILE: Stories_0ae089fca6 [Librarium Cthulhuvius_3.txt].txt
Mentions: 1/1 | d:1.22/10k

[1] Йог-Сотот (The Lurker at the Threshold) L55 [Мифологическое описание]
S. T. Joshi has published his reading of the text in H. P. Lovecraft, Collected Fiction Volume 3 (1931-1936): A Variorum Edition. Joshi suggests the fragment is from the mid-1930s. The title Of Evill Sorceries done in New England, of Daemons in No Humane Shape occurs at the beginning of the first page, and the publishing information for Thaumaturgical Prodigies in the New-English Canaan occurs on the final page. Joshi interprets Of Evill Sorceries as being an extract from the longer work Thaumaturgical Prodigies. When August Derleth adapted this fragment for use in his novel The Lurker at the Threshold, he broke the text into two pieces. He labeled the first section as Of Evill Sorceries done in New England, of Daemons in No Humane Shape. However, he treated the final page as an extract from a separate work, Thaumaturgical Prodigies in the New-English Canaan. This is a conceivable interpretation since the title Thaumaturgical Prodigies appears only on the final page of the manuscript.

His mind was tired, but I am always a German, and was quick to notice two things; that the U-29 was standing the deep-sea pressure splendidly, and that the peculiar dolphins were still about us, even at a depth where the existence of high organisms is considered impossible by most naturalists. That I had previously overestimated our depth, I was sure; but none the less we must still be deep enough to make these phenomena remarkable.

Toward morning I must have dropped asleep with the lights on, for I awoke in darkness yesterday afternoon to find the batteries dead. I struck several matches in succession, and desperately regretted the improvidence which had caused us long ago to use up the few candles we carried. After the fading of the last match I dared to waste, I sat very quietly without a light. [4] Тьма (The Darkness) L97 [Мифологическое описание]
I must be careful how I record my awaking today, for I am unstrung, and much hallucination is necessarily mixed with fact. Psychologically my case is most interesting, and I regret that it cannot be observed scientifically by a competent German authority. Upon opening my eyes my first sensation was an overmastering desire to visit the rock temple; a desire which grew every instant, yet which I automatically sought to resist through some emotion of fear which operated in the reverse direction. Next there came to me the impression of light amidst the darkness of dead batteries, and I seemed to see a sort of phosphorescent glow in the water through the porthole which opened toward the temple. This aroused my curiosity, for I knew of no deep-sea organism capable of emitting such luminosity. But before I could investigate there came a third impression which because of its irrationality caused me to doubt the objectivity of anything my senses might record. It was an aural delusion; a sensation of rhythmic, melodic sound as of some wild yet beautiful chant or choral hymn, coming from the outside through the absolutely sound-proof hull of the U-29.

Sir Wade was, indeed, most peculiar in his solicitude for his family; for when he returned to Africa he would permit no one to care for his young son save a loathsome black woman from Guinea. Upon coming back, after the death of Lady Jermyn, he himself assumed complete care of the boy. But it was the talk of Sir Wade, especially when in his cups, which chiefly led his friends to deem him mad. In a rational age like the eighteenth century it was unwise for a man of learning to talk about wild sights and strange scenes under a Congo moon; of the gigantic walls and pillars of a forgotten city, crumbling and vine-grown, and of damp, silent, stone steps leading interminably down into the darkness of abysmal treasure-vaults and inconceivable catacombs. Especially was it unwise to rave of the living things that might haunt such a place; of creatures half of the jungle and half of the impiously aged city—fabulous creatures which even a Pliny might describe with scepticism; things that might have sprung up after the great apes had overrun the dying city with the walls and the pillars, the vaults and the weird carvings.

Moore: George Campbell opened sleep-fogged eyes upon darkness and lay gazing out of the tent flap upon the pale August night for some minutes before he roused enough even to wonder what had wakened him. Every standard of speed known to earth seemed dwarfed, and Campbell knew that any such flight in physical reality would mean instant death to a human being. If so, though, the nightmare must still be in force; since his present apparently bodiless state had nothing of normality in it. Of the time consumed by this puzzled memory and reflection, Campbell could form no estimate. Everything about his state was so unreal that ordinary dimensions and measurements became meaningless. It seemed an eternity, but perhaps it was not really long before the sudden interruption came. What happened was as strange and inexplicable as the blackness it succeeded.

Around me were the tombs and the darkness and the shadows; below me, some peril beyond the radius of the human imagination. But as the gate swung wider and the sorcery of drug and dream pushed me through, I knew that all sights and glories were at an end; for in that new realm was neither land nor sea, but only the white void of unpeopled and illimitable space. So, happier than I had ever dared hoped to be, I dissolved again into that native infinity of crystal oblivion from which the daemon Life had called me for one brief and desolate hour. [1] Тьма (Darkness) L39 [Художественный сюжет]
Vaughan FROM BETWEEN THE STAR-SPACES by James Ambuehl THE CTHULHU MYTHOS, by August Derleth. New York: Barnes & Noble, 1997. 448 pp. $9.98. 0-7607-0253-5. (Note: Mr. Kaye paid $7.98 for his copy. -- Ed.) [Reviewed by Steven Kaye] This was originally posted in the alt. horror. cthulhu newsgroup. The stories included in this volume are all the "noncollaborative" tales -- those looking for "Lair of the Star-Spawn," "Lurker on the Threshold," etc. should look elsewhere. The first section, titled THE DERLETH MYTHOS, includes "The Dweller in Darkness," "Beyond the Threshold," "The Thing That Walked on the Wind," "Ithaqua," "The Passing of Eric Holm," and "Something From Out There." "Dweller" explicitly mentions the elemental theory (each of the Old Ones being associated with a certain element -- Cthulhu with water, Hastur with air, etc.) . I'm not sure if this is the first instance -- Derleth scholars care to comment? Two friends go to Rick's Lake to investigate the disappearance of their friend, and come upon Things Man Was Not Meant to Know.

[2] Тьма (Darkness) L43 [Гримуар]
. I'm not sure if this is the first instance -- Derleth scholars care to comment? Two friends go to Rick's Lake to investigate the disappearance of their friend, and come upon Things Man Was Not Meant to Know. Derleth sprinkles the story liberally with pastiches of Lovecraft (compare the opening sentence with that of "The Dunwich Horror"). There is also a near-quote from Supernatural Horror in Literature and a transcript reminiscent of "The Whisperer in Darkness." Jack is written as a bit of a dunce, in order for Laird Dorgan to deliver the exposition. There is also the signature "let's explain the events of the story in the final paragraph in excruciating detail, all in italics, just in case the reader wasn't paying attention." The plot of the story is compelling, if derivative of "Whisperer," but Derleth's reluctant to stand on his own.

[3] Йог-Сотот (The Key) L71 [Энциклопедическая статья]
Ultimately flawed, but an interesting attempt. "The Seal of R'lyeh" is frustrating, in that the first sentence gives away the entire story. It's also frustrating to find R'lyeh arbitrarily shifting between the Atlantic and Pacific, although I suppose Derleth could have been trying for something like the bilocation of Leng or Kadath. Too little new of interest -- the same references to Lovecraft stories, overused plot elements, etc. The final section is The Trail of Cthulhu - "The House on Curwen Street," "The Watcher from the Sky," "The Gorge Beyond Salapunco," "The Keeper of the Key," and "The Black Island." Unlike The Mask of Cthulhu (which was a collection of unrelated stories), Trail is actually a series of linked stories about Dr. Laban Shrewsbury and his attempts to rid the world of the threat of Cthulhu. As such, I'll review the stories as a whole. Plot summary: Thick young man knowing nothing of the Mythos encounters Dr. Shrewsbury (or one of his assistants), they encounter a Mythos threat, massive explosions ensue, something comes after the thick young man and . .

[1] Йог-Сотот (Yog-Sothoth) L33
Derleth runs into many contradictions here. For instance, he makes Cthulhu and his minions water beings, whereas "The Call of Cthulhu" has them coming down from space and building their cities on land; only later are their cities submerged by geological upheavals, and this is a catastrophe which immobilizes the Cthulhu spawn. Hastur is portrayed as an "air elemental," while at the same time Derleth implies that he lives on the bottom of the lake of Hali. Yog-Sothoth and Nyarlathotep, probably the two more purely Cosmic of all Lovecraftian entities, are squeezed into the "earth" category; while, finally, he invents the fire elemental, Cthugha, to round out his menagerie of elementals. (Lovecraft invented no beings that could be construed as "fire elementals.") Cthugha comes from the star Fomalhaut -- presumably because Lovecraft once mentioned that star in one of his sonnets. Elementals aside, the whole basic concept of Derleth's "good-versus-evil" Mythos seems as non-Lovecraftian as anything conceivable. Lovecraft actually regarded the Cosmos as basically indifferent to anthropocentric outlooks such as good and evil.

I asked him to send it, I loved it, and it became the cover as shown above. In the summer of 1971 I was thinking of a portfolio of 13 pieces and some mimeographed text by Meade and Penny as a little "zine" of tribute, just another item of our amateur press publications. I had asked Steve Fabian, Dany Frolich and Herb Arnold to try some Lovecraft story interpretations, too. Now, back to the worldcon. After a boozy day in the bar, what happened the next morning? It was so good that it had to be in a better publication than I had been thinking about; it had to be part of that grander tribute that Tom Collins was urging. What about articles and fiction for this grander tribute? In September 1971 there were none. Who did I know? I had addresses of Southern fans, including that of Manly Wade Wellman -- how about reprinting a Cthulhu Mythos story by him? Permission was granted for "The Terrible Parchment."

My goal in assembling the present collection is, in effect, to go back and do again what August Derleth did: to assemble a flagship Mythos collection that he might as well have assembled. It is an alternate version of Tales of the Cthulhu Mythos The editor notes that the book "covers the pulp era, but extends no further. We are concerned here with the foundational generation of Mythos writers." It also is an attempt to "assemble the stories in which certain important Mythos names or items are either first mentioned or most fully explained by the author who created them": here you will find the truth that had hitherto been mercifully cloaked beneath the mystifying names Abhoth Atlach-Nacha Unter Zee Kulten Hydrophinnae , the Eltdown Shards ’Umr at-Tawil Lloigor Zhar , the Tcho-Tcho people Ithaqua Iod Vorvadoss Zuchequan , the Chronicle of Nath , and others. Several of the stories in the collection appear in earlier forms that differ significantly from later revisions--including "The Lord of Illusion", the original draft of the story that became the H. P. Lovecraft/E. Hoffman Price collaboration " Through the Gates of the Silver Key Price's subsequent anthology The New Lovecraft Circle serves as a sequel of sorts to Tales of the Lovecraft Mythos , collecting work from the next generation of Lovecraftian writers. FILE: Tcho-Tcho people.txt
Mentions: 1/1 | d:3.33/10k

[1] Наг и Йеб (Zhar and Lloigor) L73 [Мифологическое описание]
Created by August Derleth and Mark Schorer The Tcho-Tcho people are a fictional species of hominids in the Cthulhu Mythos . They were originally created by August Derleth and Mark Schorer for their short story " The Lair of the Star-Spawn Background The Tcho-Tcho people are a group of tribes of near-human beings native to Asia. They can be found in Burma, The Anderman Isles, Tibet, and Malaysia. They are genetically from humans, but they are notably smaller, have livid red skin, and other marked physiological differences. Legends point to prehistoric genetic engineering of pre-human ancestors by the Great Old Ones Zhar and Lloigor . These legends purport they "grew from the 'seeds' of the Twin Obscenities". The Tcho-Tcho people are feared by other tribes and appear to be inimical to Mankind, while worshiping various deities including Han Chaugnar Faugn Rhan-Tegoth Hastur and his spawn. They appear to be the "corpse-eating cult of Leng" mentioned in the Necronomicon and have "lamas" as priests (cf. Elder Hierophant ). One source suggests that only the warrior caste are bred small. They might be related to the Men of Leng in the Dreamlands .

НАЗВАНИЕ: Terror of Cut-Throat Cove (Cthulhu Universalis) ИСТОЧНИК: Terror of Cut-Throat Cove RB Terror ]: A creature of darkness that seeks to "devour the world." It was once worshipped by a valley people in the jungles south of Venezuela . It rested in a great golden ark or chest with an altar of beaten gold in front of it. The creature would emerge when the locals offered it sacrifices: first captives, then slaves, then children, then their choicest virgins. Eventually the natives sealed the lid. Later, conquistadors conquered the natives and sought to take the chest and altar back to Spain aboard the Santa Maria in 1711.

[3] Йог-Сотот (Той) L41 [Художественный сюжет]
Многие пленники погибали в этих горьких переходах. Другие начинали новую жизнь, никогда больше не видя ни старых домов, ни семей. Третьих, говоря языком того времени, "выкупали" — возвращали семьям, но редко в родные дома. Ремембранс Тайлер не была ни выкуплена, ни возвращена. Историки не обнаружили ни единого свидетельства или документа о том, чтобы женщина с таким именем вышла замуж или родила в далёких католических дебрях Канады. Многие предполагали, что Ремембранс погибла в пути. Но никто из живых не знал правды. Поколения той эпохи давно уже приложились к отцам своим. Покумтуки вымерли в 1700-х годах. Некому было рассказать её историю. И всё же Ремембранс Тайлер никогда полностью не забывали. Мало кто мог прийти к согласию насчёт того, когда впервые заметили фигуру в чепце с оборкой, неверной поступью пробиравшуюся среди извилистых оврагов и глубоких впадин к северо-востоку от Фоксфилда. Первые сообщения, как и следовало ожидать, были устными. Одни говорили — 1753 год. Другие клялись, что фантома светлячков впервые встретили не ранее 1777 года. Самое раннее задокументированное наблюдение (если употребить современное слово) относится к 1779 году.

[4] Тьма (Тьму) L63 [Ритуал и призывание]
В конце XIX века (время растущего интереса к спиритизму) некоторые собирались на восточной стороне ущелья, чтобы "привести Ремембранс домой". Стеклянные банки, наполненные вялыми жучками-светлячками, служили свечами в этих безобидных обрядах. Эти действа с перерывами продолжались около трёх лет. Только однажды нечто похожее на волнение нарушило безмятежный ритуал. Это случилось в ночь на 28 апреля 1894 года. Пастыри Ремембранс, как их называли, пробирались среди облезающих бумажных берёз и робиний ложноакациевых, когда чепец с оборкой (к тому времени безнадёжно вышедший из моды) снова был узнан. Разнеслась весть. Раздались оклики. Во тьму густого леса полетели мольбы. Они призывали Ремембранс пойти по южному ответвлению тропы к новому крытому мосту и оставить ту, что больше не пересекала коварное ущелье Пассикуамстук. Услышала ли Ремембранс (если это действительно была она) или поняла — так и осталось неизвестным. Та, что в чепце с оборкой, бежала. Пастыри Ремембранс больше её не видели — хотя сама группа просуществовала до 1897 года. Наблюдения продолжались и в начале XX века, но к ним относились всё менее серьёзно. Магистрали расширялись. Автомобили и поезда неумолимо катились через долину Мискатоник, отбрасывая прочь ужас и суеверия.

Mentions: 1/1 | d:5.96/10k

[1] Тьма (Darkness) L55 [Мифологическое описание]
Synopsis An expedition from the California Historical Society working near the town of San Xavier, California , unearths a trio of bells said to summon a dread entity when rung. Despite the horrific incidents which occur during their removal - including one of the local attendants gouging out his own eyes - the group brings the bells back to San Xavier and has them hung in the local Mission. There, an earthquake causes the bells to begin ringing, and a darkness descends over the eyes of all who hear it. Only the members of the Historical Society, with their knowledge of the occult grimoire The Book of Iod , are able to stop the bells and restore sight and sanity to the town. However, a solar eclipse two months later appears to precipitate a gruesome suicide, and brings the suggestion that the summoning of the bells was not as unsuccessful as the party had previously thought . . . Characters Ross , secretary of the California Historical Society. Arthur Todd , president of the society. Denton , Todd's assistant.

P. Lovecraft Overview First published in October 1982 by Del Rey/Ballantine, The Best of H. P. Lovecraft: Bloodcurdling Tales of Horror and the Macabre contains a total of 16 of Lovecraft's most prominent works and is prefaced by an introduction from one of Lovecraft’s protégés, the late American author Robert Bloch , with cover art supplied by Michael Whelan. It was reprinted in September 1988 and April 1995, and received an ebook release in November 2002.
